**The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, saying: ﴿And We brought the others near there﴾**

By His saying, may He be remembered: ﴿And We brought the others near there﴾, it means: We drew the family of Pharaoh near to the sea and brought them forward to it. From the same root is His saying: ﴿And Paradise will be brought near for the righteous﴾, meaning: brought close and made near. From the same usage is the verse of al-'Ajjaj:

*Through the nights, stage after stage, he folded them, / the high ridge of the crescent, until it bent.* [[The verse is from the rajaz meter, and both lines are by al-'Ajjaj, from a long rajaz poem of his describing his journey through the shadows of the night, and a swift camel that carried him. (See Lisan al-'Arab, entry zlf; and Al-Sayyid al-Bakri, Arajiz al-'Arab, p. 52.) Before the two lines there is a line connected in meaning to them, which is his saying: "A swift one whom weariness folded and the distance wore down."*

Ibn Manzur said in Lisan al-'Arab: He means one station after another, and one degree after another. Al-Sayyid al-Bakri said: "Zulfan fa-zulfa" means degree after degree. "Sama'a" means high. "Ihqawqafa" means bent. He means that travel folded him as the nights fold the crescents until they wane (from nuhul, emaciation) and become bent. End. In Lisan al-'Arab: "Zulf" (on the pattern of sabab), "zulfa" and "zulfa" mean nearness, degree, and station. "Azlafa al-shay'" means he brought it near. In the Revelation (in the verse "and Paradise was brought near for the righteous") it means brought near. Al-Zajjaj said: Its interpretation is that their entry into it and their gazing at it are near. As for His saying, mighty and majestic: ﴿And We brought the others near there﴾, the meaning of "azlafna" is "gathered," and it was said: "We brought the others near to drowning," meaning Pharaoh's people. Both are good and beautiful, because gathering them is bringing some of them near to others. The two lines are among the evidences cited by Abu 'Ubayda in Majaz al-Qur'an (p. 172 of the Cairo University manuscript). [[End of editor's note.]]

The people of ta'wil (interpretation, tafsir) said something similar to what we have said.

**Those who said that:**

- Al-Qasim narrated to me, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from 'Ata' al-Khurasani, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿And We brought the others near there﴾, he said: "We brought them near."

- Al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatada, regarding His saying: ﴿And We brought the others near there﴾, he said: "They are the people of Pharaoh. God brought them near until He drowned them in the sea."

- Musa narrated to us, saying: 'Amr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, who said: Pharaoh and his companions drew near after Musa had led the Children of Israel across the sea. When Pharaoh saw the sea split open, he said: "Do you not see the sea split apart before me? It has opened for me so that I may catch up with my enemies and kill them." That is the saying of God: ﴿And We brought the others near there﴾, meaning: We brought them near. The others are the family of Pharaoh. When Pharaoh stood at the crossings, his horses refused to plunge in. Gabriel (peace be upon him) descended upon a mare, and the horses caught her scent and rushed in after her. When the first of them was about to come out and the last of them had entered, He commanded the sea to seize them, and it closed over them. Gabriel alone was left with a handful of the sea's clay, which he began to push into his mouth.

- Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Abu Bakr ibn 'Abd Allah, who said: Pharaoh advanced, and when he came within sight of the water, the companions of Musa said: "O one who was spoken to by God, the people are following us on the road. Strike the sea with your staff and make it churn." Musa wished to do so, but God revealed to him: "Leave the sea at rest" (rahwan), meaning: leave it in its calm state. "Indeed they are an army to be drowned." I am only tricking them; when they take your path, I will drown them. When Pharaoh looked at the sea, he said: "Do you not see the sea split apart before me, so that it opens for me, so that I may catch up with my enemies and kill them?" When he stood at the mouths of the paths, mounted on a stallion, the stallion saw the sea with what looked like mountains in it, and it recoiled and was afraid. Pharaoh said: "I am turning back." Gabriel, peace be upon him, then deceived him. He came on a female horse and brought her close to Pharaoh's stallion. Pharaoh's horse began not to stand still, and Gabriel kept saying: "Go forward," and saying: "No one has a better right to the road than you." Then the stallion was drawn to the mare, and Pharaoh could not restrain his horse from plunging in after her. When Pharaoh reached the middle of the sea, God revealed to the sea: "Seize My servant the wrongdoer and My servants who are oppressors. My authority is over you, for I have given you power over them." He said: The waves rose up like mountains, and they struck one another. When drowning overtook him, [He said]: ﴿I believe that there is no god except the One in whom the Children of Israel believe, and I am among the Muslims﴾. Gabriel, peace be upon him, was greatly grieved over him because of the signs of God that he had rejected, and because of the long time Musa had spent dealing with him. So he entered the bottom of the sea, brought up mud, and stuffed it into Pharaoh's mouth, lest he say it a second time, and so that mercy would not reach him. He said: Then God sent Michael to rebuke him: ﴿Now? And you had disobeyed before and were among the corrupters﴾. Gabriel said: "O Muhammad, I have never hated any of God's creatures as I hated two: one of them from the jinn, namely Iblis, and the other Pharaoh, ﴿who said: I am your lord, the most high﴾." "And you would have seen me, O Muhammad, as I stuffed it into his mouth, fearing that he would say a word by which God might have mercy on him."

Some of them claimed that the meaning of His saying: ﴿And We brought the others near there﴾ is "and We gathered." He said: From this comes the night of Muzdalifa, meaning that it is the night of gathering (jam'). Some of them said: "And We brought them near there" means "and We destroyed them."

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And We delivered Musa and those with him, all of them﴾

May He be remembered, says: We delivered Musa from what We had caused to pursue Pharaoh and his people, namely drowning in the sea, and We delivered those with Musa from the Children of Israel, all of them.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Then We drowned the others﴾

He says: Then We drowned Pharaoh and his people, the Copts, in the sea, after We had delivered Musa and those with him from it.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Indeed in that is a sign﴾

May He be remembered, says: Indeed, in what I did to Pharaoh and those with him, by drowning them in the sea, because they denied My messenger Musa and opposed My command after the warning and admonition given to them, there is a clear proof, O Muhammad, for your people of Quraysh, that this is My practice toward those who follow their path in denying My messengers. It is also an admonition and a lesson for them, so that they may take heed and reflect, lest they do what they did by denying you despite the proof and signs that have come to them, and so that the same punishment that befell them will befall them. And for you there is a sign in My dealing with Musa, and My delivering him after Pharaoh and his people had long opposed him, and My making him and his people inherit their homes, lands, and wealth. I will likewise make you follow his path, if you endure as he endured, and rise to convey the message to those to whom I send you, as he rose, and I will make you prevail over those who deny you and make you superior to them. ﴿And most of them were not believers﴾: He says: Most of your people, O Muhammad, were not believers in the clear truth that God brought you. So it had already been decreed in My knowledge that they would not believe.

﴿And indeed your Lord is the Mighty﴾ in His vengeance against those who disbelieved in Him and denied His messengers among His enemies, ﴿the Merciful﴾ toward those among His messengers and their followers whom He delivered from drowning and from the punishment with which He punished the disbelievers.

When the first of them was about to come out and the last of them had entered, He commanded the sea to seize them, and it closed over them. Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 26, verse 75–77:

The interpretation of His saying, ﴿He said: "Have you considered what you have been worshipping, you and your forefathers, the ancient ones? For indeed, they are enemies to me, except the Lord of the worlds."﴾

Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Abraham said to his people: "Have you considered, O people, what you have been worshipping of these idols, you and your forefathers, the ancient ones?" By "the ancient ones" he means the ancients among those whom Abraham was addressing, namely those before them who were upon the same worship of idols as those whom Abraham spoke to. ﴿For indeed, they are enemies to me, except the Lord of the worlds.﴾ One may say: How can wood, iron and copper be described as enemies of the son of Adam? The meaning of that is: they will be enemies to me if I worship them on the Day of Resurrection, as His majestic praise says: ﴿And they have taken besides Allah gods that they might be for them a source of honour. No! They will reject their worship of them and will be opposed to them.﴾

* *

As for His saying: ﴿except the Lord of the worlds﴾

It is in the accusative as an exception, and "enemy" (ʿaduww) is used in the sense of a plural, and it is in the singular because it is expressed in the form of a verbal noun (maṣdar), like "al-quʿūd" (sitting) and "al-julūs" (sitting).

The meaning of the statement: "Have you considered every object of worship that you and your forefathers have had? Indeed, I am free of it and do not worship it, except the Lord of the worlds."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 26, verses 78–82:

The interpretation of His words, the Exalted: ﴿Who created me, and it is He who guides me﴾ (78) ﴿And who feeds me and gives me drink﴾ (79) ﴿And when I am ill, it is He who cures me﴾ (80).

He says: "They are an enemy to me, except the Lord of the worlds." ﴿Who created me, and it is He who guides me﴾ to what is right in speech and action, and makes me firm upon rectitude. ﴿And who feeds me and gives me drink﴾ means: who nourishes me with food and drink, and provides me with sustenance. ﴿And when I am ill, it is He who cures me﴾ means: when my body becomes sick and ailing, it is He who restores it to health and grants it well-being.

* *

The interpretation of His words, the Exalted: ﴿And who causes me to die and then will bring me to life﴾ (81) ﴿And who I hope will forgive me my sin on the Day of Recompense﴾ (82).

He says: "And the One who causes me to die when He wills and then brings me to life when He wills after my death." ﴿And who I hope will forgive me my sin on the Day of Recompense﴾: my Lord is He in whose hand is my benefit and my harm, who possesses power and dominion, and to whom belong this world and the Hereafter, not the one who does not hear when called upon, nor benefits, nor harms. This speech of Abraham was indeed an argument against his people, that divinity is not fitting and worship is not due except to one who does these acts, not to one who is unable to bring benefit or harm.

It has also been said: Abraham, may the blessings of God be upon him, meant by his words ﴿And who I hope will forgive me my sin on the Day of Recompense﴾: "the One whom I hope will forgive me for my saying ﴿I am sick﴾ and his saying ﴿Rather, it was done by this, their chief﴾ and my saying to Sarah: she is my sister."

Mention of those who said this:

⁕ Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding the words of God: ﴿that He forgive me my sin on the Day of Recompense﴾, he said: [it refers to] his saying ﴿I am sick﴾, and his saying ﴿it was done by this, their chief﴾, and his saying to Sarah: she is my sister, when one of the Pharaohs wanted to take her.

The exegesis of His words, ﴿My Lord, grant me judgment and join me with the righteous﴾ (83), and ﴿Grant me a true tongue of praise among the later generations﴾ (84).

Exalted is He, mentioning the request of His friend Ibrahim (Abraham) to Him, ﴿My Lord, grant me judgment﴾. He says: "My Lord, grant me prophethood." ﴿And join me with the righteous﴾ means: "Make me a messenger to Your creation, so that I am joined with those whom You have sent as messengers to Your creation, whom You have entrusted with Your revelation and chosen for Yourself."

* *

As for His words, ﴿And grant me a true tongue of praise among the later generations﴾:

He means: "Grant me a good remembrance and a fine praise among the people, lasting among those generations that come after me."

The people of ta'wil (interpretation of the Qur'an) have said the like of what we have said about this.

Mention of those who said that:

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Abu Bakr, from Ikrimah, regarding His words, ﴿And grant me a true tongue of praise among the later generations﴾, and His words, ﴿And We gave him his reward in this world﴾. He said: Indeed Allah favoured him with friendship (khullah) when He took him as a friend (khalil), so he asked Allah, saying, ﴿And grant me a true tongue of praise among the later generations﴾, so that the nations would not deny me. Allah granted him that. The Jews believed in Musa (Moses) and disbelieved in Isa (Jesus), and the Christians believed in Isa and disbelieved in Muhammad (ﷺ), yet all of them claim allegiance to Ibrahim. The Jews said: "He is the friend of Allah and he is one of us." So Allah cut off their allegiance to him after they had acknowledged his prophethood and believed in him, and He said: ﴿Abraham was neither a Jew nor a Christian, but he was a true monotheist (hanif), a Muslim, and he was not of the polytheists﴾. Then He joined his allegiance to you, saying: ﴿Indeed, the people most worthy of Abraham are those who followed him, and this Prophet, and those who believe, and Allah is the Protector of the believers﴾. This is his reward that was hastened for him, and it is the good name (al-hasanah), when He says: ﴿And We gave him in this world a good name﴾, and it is the true tongue that he asked his Lord for.

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words, ﴿And grant me a true tongue of praise among the later generations﴾: The true tongue is a true remembrance, a righteous praise, and a righteous remembrance among the later people, among the nations.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 26, verses 90–95:

The interpretation of His statement, exalted is He: ﴿And Paradise will be brought near for the God-fearing﴾

He, may His praise be exalted, means by His words: ﴿And Paradise will be brought near for the God-fearing﴾: Paradise will be drawn near and brought close to the God-fearing, those who guarded themselves against the punishment of God in the Hereafter by obeying Him in this world. ﴿And Hellfire will be made apparent to the misguided﴾: he says, the Fire will be made visible to those who went astray and deviated from the right path. ﴿And it will be said to them: "Where is that which you used to worship besides God?"﴾ from among the rivals, ﴿"Can they help you, or help themselves?"﴾ today, against God, so that they might rescue you from His punishment, ﴿or help themselves,﴾ so that they might save themselves from what is intended for them?

* *

As for His statement: ﴿Then they will be thrown into it, they and the misguided.﴾

He says: some of them will be hurled into Hellfire upon others, and some will be cast down upon others, falling headlong on their faces. The original form of "kubkibu" is "kubbibu," but the letter kaf was repeated, as is said in the words ﴿with a violent screaming wind﴾, where what is meant is "sarr" (the root form), and in "yunahnihuni" (he keeps me back), what is meant is "nahhani" (he restrains me).

The interpreters of the Qur'an have said something similar to what we have said on this matter.

So the meaning of the statement is: these rivals that were worshipped besides God, and the misguided, will be cast headlong into Hellfire.

He means: By Allah, we were indeed straying from the truth, in clear error, which their straying from it, for whoever reflects and ponders over it, makes plain to them that it is error and falsehood.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿when we equated you with the Lord of the worlds﴾

The misguided ones say to those they used to worship besides Allah: By Allah, we were indeed straying from the truth when we equated you with the Lord of the worlds, and so worshipped you besides Him.

Those who engage in ta'wil (interpretation of the Qur'an) have said what we have said regarding this.

Mention of those who said that:

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying: ﴿when we equated you with the Lord of the worlds﴾: "[It refers] to those deities."

On the interpretation of His words, ﴿And none led us astray except the criminals﴾:

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says, reporting the words of those deviators in Hellfire: ﴿And none led us astray except the criminals﴾, meaning by the criminals Iblis and the son of Adam who instituted killing.

As related:

* Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Ikrimah, regarding His words ﴿And none led us astray except the criminals﴾, he said: Iblis and the son of Adam, the killer.

* *

That is, there is no intercessor for us who would intercede for us with God from among those close to us, so that He would pardon us and save us from His punishment. ﴿Nor a close friend﴾ from among the relatives.

**The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿Indeed in that is a sign, but most of them were not believers (103) And indeed your Lord is the Mighty, the Merciful (104)﴾**

Almighty God says: Indeed, in what Ibrahim argued against his people of the proofs we mentioned to him is a clear and manifest evidence for whoever takes heed, that God's practice with His creation, toward those who follow the practice of the people of Ibrahim in worshipping idols and deities and imitate them in that, is what He has decreed for them in the Hereafter: their being hurled headlong (kabkabah) into Hell, along with them what they worshipped besides Him, together with the armies of Iblis. And most of them, in His prior knowledge, were not believers. And indeed your Lord, O Muhammad, is the Severe in retribution against whoever worships other than Him and then does not repent of his disbelief until he dies, and the Merciful toward whoever of them repents, by not punishing him for the sin and crime that he committed before his repentance.

* *

**The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿The people of Nuh denied the messengers (105) When their brother Nuh said to them, "Will you not fear God?" (106) Indeed I am a trustworthy messenger to you (107)﴾**

Almighty God says: ﴿The people of Nuh denied﴾ the messengers of God whom He sent to them, when ﴿their brother Nuh said to them, "Will you not fear God?"﴾ so that you might beware of His punishment for your disbelief in Him and your denial of His messengers. ﴿Indeed I am a messenger﴾ from God ﴿trustworthy﴾ concerning His revelation to me, in His sending me to you with His message.

* *

**The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿So fear God and obey me (108) And I do not ask you for any wage for it; my wage is only from the Lord of the worlds (109) So fear God and obey me (110)﴾**

Almighty God says: So fear the punishment of God, O people, for your disbelief in Him, and obey me in my counsel to you and my command to you to guard against His punishment by obeying Him in what He has commanded and forbidden you. ﴿And I do not ask you for any wage for it﴾ means: I do not seek from you any reward or recompense for my counsel to you and my command to you to guard against God's punishment by obeying Him. ﴿My wage is only from the Lord of the worlds﴾, apart from you and apart from all of God's creation. So fear God's punishment for your disbelief in Him, and fear the descent of His wrath upon you for your denial of His messengers. ﴿And obey me﴾: that is, obey me in my counsel to you and my command to you to devote worship sincerely to your Creator.

So fear God's punishment for your disbelief in Him, and fear the descent of His wrath upon you for your denial of His messengers. ﴿And obey me﴾: that is, obey me in my counsel to you and my command to you to devote worship sincerely to your Creator.

And indeed your Lord, O Muhammad, is the Severe in retribution against whoever worships other than Him and then does not repent of his disbelief until he dies, and the Merciful toward whoever of them repents, by not punishing him for the sin and crime that he committed before his repentance.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 26, verse 111–116:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿They said, "Shall we believe you, when the lowest [of the people] follow you?" (111) He said, "And what is my knowledge of what they used to do? (112) Their account is only upon my Lord, if you were aware. (113)"﴾

His saying, exalted is His remembrance: The people of Noah, responding to him after his statement to them, ﴿"Indeed, I am to you a trustworthy messenger, so fear Allah and obey me"﴾, said: "Shall we believe you, O Noah, and affirm your truthfulness in what you call us to, when only the lowest among us follow you, to the exclusion of those of nobility and houses of distinction?" ﴿He said, "And what is my knowledge of what they used to do?"﴾ Noah said to his people: "And what is my knowledge of what my followers were doing? I have from them only the outward appearance of their affairs, not their inner state, and I was not charged with knowing their inner state; I was charged only with the outward. So whoever shows good, I assume good of him, and whoever shows evil, I assume evil of him." He says: "Their account concerning the inner state of their affairs, which is hidden from me, is only upon my Lord, if you were aware, for He knows the secret and the open of their affairs."

Similar to what we have said on this, the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said.

Mention of those who said this:

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, regarding His saying: ﴿Their account is only upon my Lord, if you were aware﴾, he said: "He is more knowing of what is in their souls."

As it has been narrated:

* Al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, concerning His words: ﴿So judge decisively between me and them﴾ he said: "Decide between me and them with a decision."

* Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His words: ﴿So judge decisively between me and them﴾ he said: He says, "Decide between me and them." ﴿And deliver me﴾ means: deliver me from that punishment which You bring, as a judgment between me and them. ﴿And those of the believers who are with me﴾ means: and those who are with me of the people of faith in You and of belief in me.

* * *

And His words: ﴿So We saved him and those with him in the laden ship.﴾

He says: So We saved Noah and those of the believers who were with him, when We judged between them and their people and sent down Our punishment upon the disbelieving people, in the laden ship, meaning the ship that was heavily loaded and filled.

The people of interpretation said in accordance with what we have said concerning the interpretation of His words ﴿the laden ship﴾.

Those who said that:

* Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His words: ﴿in the laden ship﴾ he said: meaning the heavily loaded one.

* Muhammad ibn Sinan al-Qazzaz narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan al-Ashqar narrated to us, saying: Abu Kudaynah narrated to us, from 'Ata', from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "al-Mashhun": the heavily loaded.

* Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning the words of God: ﴿the laden ship﴾ he said: the completely loaded and filled.

* al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, who said: "al-Mashhun": completely loaded with cargo.

* al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, concerning the words of God: ﴿the laden ship﴾ he said: it is the carrier (al-mahmal).

* Al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, concerning His words: ﴿So judge decisively between me and them﴾ he said: "Decide between me and them with a decision."

* Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His words: ﴿So judge decisively between me and them﴾ he said: He says, "Decide between me and them." ﴿And deliver me﴾ means: deliver me from that punishment which You bring, as a judgment between me and them. ﴿And those of the believers who are with me﴾ means: and those who are with me of the people of faith in You and of belief in me.

* * *

He says: So We saved Noah and those of the believers who were with him, when We judged between them and their people and sent down Our punishment upon the disbelieving people, in the laden ship, meaning the ship that was heavily loaded and filled.

* Muhammad ibn Sinan al-Qazzaz narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan al-Ashqar narrated to us, saying: Abu Kudaynah narrated to us, from 'Ata', from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "al-Mashhun": the heavily loaded.

* Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning the words of God: ﴿the laden ship﴾ he said: the completely loaded and filled.

* al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, who said: "al-Mashhun": completely loaded with cargo.

* al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, concerning the words of God: ﴿the laden ship﴾ he said: it is the carrier (al-mahmal).

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 26, verses 121–127:

The interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed in that is a sign, but most of them were not believers. And indeed, your Lord is the Exalted in Might, the Merciful.﴾

Says God, may His remembrance be exalted: Indeed, in what We did, O Muhammad, with Noah and those who were with him among the believers in the laden ship, when We sent down Our punishment and Our might upon his people who denied him, there is a sign for you and for your people, both those among them who confirm you and those who deny you, concerning the fact that Our way is to save Our messengers and their followers when Our vengeance descends upon those among their people who deny them, and to destroy those who deny God. And so is My way with you and your people. ﴿And most of them were not believers﴾ means: and most of your people were not among those who would confirm you, according to what had already preceded in God's decree, that they would never believe. ﴿And indeed, your Lord is the Exalted in Might﴾ in His retribution against those who disbelieve in Him and oppose His command, ﴿the Merciful﴾ toward those among them who repent, so that He does not punish them after their repentance.

* *

The interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿The people of ʿAd denied the messengers. When their brother Hud said to them, "Will you not fear God? Indeed, I am to you a trustworthy messenger. So fear God and obey me. And I do not ask of you any wage for it; my wage is only from the Lord of the worlds."﴾

Says God, may His remembrance be exalted: ﴿The people of ʿAd denied﴾ the messengers of God sent to them. ﴿When their brother Hud said to them, "Will you not fear﴾ God's punishment for your disbelief in Him?" ﴿Indeed, I am to you a messenger﴾ from my Lord, commanding you to obey Him and warning you of His might for your disbelief, ﴿trustworthy﴾ concerning His revelation and His message. ﴿So fear God﴾ by obeying Him and desisting from what He commands and forbids you, ﴿and obey me﴾ in what I command you concerning fearing God and heeding His might. (And I do not ask of you any wage for it) means: and I do not seek from you any recompense or reward for my commanding you to fear God. ﴿My wage is only from the Lord of the worlds﴾ means: my recompense and reward for my counsel to you is only from the Lord of the worlds.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 26, verse 128–130:

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿Do you build on every high place a landmark, playing?  And you take for yourselves palaces (maṣāniʿ) that you may live forever? And when you strike, you strike as tyrants.﴾ [[1]]

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says, relating the words of Hud to his people: ﴿Do you build on every high place (rīʿ) a landmark, playing?﴾ The rīʿ is every elevated place raised up from the earth, or a path, or a valley. Among the verses on this is the saying of Dhu al-Rummah:

ṭirāq al-khawāfī mushrifun fawqa rīʿatin ... nadā laylihi fī rīshihi yatarqraq [[The verse is by Dhu al-Rummah (Lisan: r-y-ʿ), who said: "al-rīʿ: a mountain, its plural being aryāʿ, rīwʿ, and riyāʿ; it is said its singular is rīʿa, and its plural riyāʿ. Ibn Barri related from Abu ʿUbayda that rīʿa is the plural of rīʿ, contrary to the statement of al-Jawhari. Dhu al-Rummah said: *ṭirāq al-khawāfī wāqiʿan fawqa rīʿa*." Also: "al-rīʿ: a road, whether travelled or not." And the Qur'anic words "bi-kulli rīʿin āyatan taʿbathūn" are recited with the rīʿ vowelled with a fatḥa (rā' with fatḥa): it is said in its explanation, "on every elevated place"; and it is said, "on every mountain pass" — al-fajj being a path opened between mountains specifically; and it is said, "on every road." Al-Farra' said: "al-rīʿ and al-rīʿ (with kasra and fatḥa of the rā') are two dialects, like al-rīr and al-rīr." End. Abu ʿUbayda said in Majaz al-Qur'an: "bi-kulli rīʿin: this is the elevation of the earth, and the road. Its plural is aryāʿ and rīʿa. Dhu al-Rummah said: ṭirāq al-khawāfī mushrifun fawqa rīʿatin ... nadā laylihi fī rīshihi yatarqraq."

In (Lisan: ṭ-r-q): "A bird with ṭirāq feathers: when some of its feathers are overlapped upon one another." Dhu al-Rummah, describing a falcon: ṭirāq al-khawāfī wāqiʿun fawqa rīʿihi ... nadā laylihi fī rīshihi yatarqraq.

Yatarqraq: it shines. Everything that has a glimmer and sheen is raqraq. Al-khawāfī: the feathers under the qawādim on a bird. Al-qawādim: plural of qādima, the four long feathers at the front of its wing.

And the saying of al-A'sha:

wa-yahmāʾu qafrin tajāwaztuhā ... idhā khabba fī rīʿihā āluhā [[The verse is attributed by the author to al-A'sha (A'sha Bani Qays ibn Thaʿlaba). In his Diwan, Cairo edition with commentary by Dr. Muhammad Husayn (pp. 163–169), there is a qasida in this metre and rhyme, of 47 verses, in praise of Iyas ibn Qabisa al-Ta'i. But the verse has fallen out of the Diwan copy, and perhaps it is found in other old copies. Yahmāʾ: a desolate waterless desert with no companion. Khabba: moved and agitated. Al-rīʿ we have explained in the preceding witness, and we related the words of the scholars. Al-āl: the mirage. Khabba al-sarāb: it moved and shone. This witness, like the one before it, the author intends that it is every elevated place raised up from the earth, or a path, or a valley, and in it are two dialects, rīʿ and rīʿ with kasra and fatḥa of the rā', as he said, and as others among the people of language said.]]

In it are two dialects: rīʿ and rayʿ, with kasra and fatḥa of the rā'.

In accordance with what we have said, the people of interpretation (ahl al-taʾwīl) said.

Those who said that:

⁕ ʿAlī related to me, he said: Abu Ṣāliḥ narrated to us, he said: Muʿāwiya related to me, from ʿAlī, from Ibn ʿAbbās, regarding His saying: ﴿Do you build on every high place a landmark, playing?﴾ He said: on every height.

⁕ Muhammad ibn ʿAmr related to me, he said: Abu ʿĀṣim narrated to us, he said: ʿĪsā narrated to us; and al-Ḥārith related to me, he said: al-Ḥasan narrated to us, he said: Warqāʾ narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najīḥ, from Mujāhid, regarding His saying: ﴿on every rīʿ﴾: he said: a mountain pass.

⁕ Muhammad ibn Saʿd related to me, he said: my father related to me, he said: my paternal uncle related to me, he said: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās, regarding His saying: ﴿Do you build on every high place a landmark﴾: he said: on every road.

⁕ al-Ḥasan narrated to us, he said: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, he said: Maʿmar informed us, from Qatāda, regarding His saying: ﴿bi-kulli rīʿ﴾: he said: on every road.

⁕ It was related to me from al-Ḥusayn, he said: I heard Abu Muʿādh say: ʿUbayd informed us, he said: I heard al-Ḍaḥḥāk say regarding His saying: ﴿bi-kulli rīʿ﴾: on every road. By His saying ﴿āya﴾ he means buildings, landmarks.

We have explained in more than one place in this book that the āya is the indication and sign, with the evidences that make repeating it here unnecessary.

In accordance with what we have said, the people of interpretation said, though they differ in their wording in its interpretation.

Those who said that:

⁕ Muhammad ibn Saʿd related to me, he said: my father related to me, he said: my paternal uncle related to me, he said: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās: ﴿bi-kulli rīʿin āya﴾: he said: the āya: a sign.

⁕ Muhammad ibn ʿAmr related to me, he said: Abu ʿĀṣim narrated to us, he said: ʿĪsā narrated to us; and al-Ḥārith related to me, he said: al-Ḥasan narrated to us, he said: Warqāʾ narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najīḥ, from Mujāhid: ﴿bi-kulli rīʿin āyatan﴾: he said: āya: buildings.

⁕ al-Qāsim narrated to us, he said: al-Ḥusayn narrated to us, he said: Ḥajjāj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujāhid: ﴿āya﴾: buildings.

And His saying: ﴿taʿbathūn﴾

He said: taliʿbūn (playing).

In accordance with what we have said in its interpretation, the people of interpretation said.

Those who said that:

⁕ Muhammad ibn Saʿd related to me, he said: my father related to me, he said: my paternal uncle related to me, he said: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās: ﴿taʿbathūn﴾: he said: you play.

⁕ It was related to me from al-Ḥusayn, he said: I heard Abu Muʿādh say: ʿUbayd informed us, he said: I heard al-Ḍaḥḥāk say regarding His saying: ﴿taʿbathūn﴾: he said: you play.

* *

And His saying: ﴿And you take for yourselves maṣāniʿ﴾

The people of interpretation differed regarding the meaning of al-maṣāniʿ. Some of them said: they are lofty palaces.

Those who said that:

⁕ Muhammad ibn ʿAmr related to me, he said: Abu ʿĀṣim narrated to us, he said: ʿĪsā narrated to us; and al-Ḥārith related to me, he said: al-Ḥasan narrated to us, he said: Warqāʾ narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najīḥ, from Mujāhid: ﴿And you take for yourselves maṣāniʿ﴾: he said: lofty palaces and everlasting buildings.

⁕ al-Qāsim narrated to us, he said: al-Ḥusayn narrated to us, he said: Ḥajjāj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujāhid: ﴿maṣāniʿ﴾: lofty palaces and buildings.

⁕ al-Ḥasan narrated to us, he said: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, he said: Maʿmar informed us, from Mujāhid, he said: ﴿maṣāniʿ﴾ means: fortresses and palaces.

⁕ Yūnus related to me, he said: Yaḥyā ibn Ḥassān informed us, from Muslim, from a man, from Mujāhid, regarding His saying: ﴿maṣāniʿa laʿallakum takhludūn﴾: he said: dovecotes.

Others said: rather, they are water reservoirs.

Those who said that:

⁕ al-Ḥasan related to me, he said: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, he said: Maʿmar informed us, from Qatāda, regarding His saying: ﴿maṣāniʿ﴾: he said: water reservoirs.

Abu Jaʿfar said: The correct view on this is to say that al-maṣāniʿ is the plural of maṣnaʿa, and the Arabs call every building a maṣnaʿa. It is possible that this building was palaces and lofty fortresses, and it is possible that it was water reservoirs, and there is no report that settles the excuse as to which of these it was, nor is it something known by reason. So the correct thing to say about it is what God said: that they used to take maṣāniʿ.

* *

He says: as if you would live forever, remaining on the earth.

In accordance with what we have said on this, the people of interpretation said.

Those who said that:

⁕ ʿAlī related to me, he said: Abu Ṣāliḥ narrated to us, he said: Muʿāwiya narrated to us, from ʿAlī, from Ibn ʿAbbās, regarding His saying: ﴿laʿallakum takhludūn﴾: he says: as if you would live forever.

⁕ al-Ḥasan narrated to us, he said: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, he said: Maʿmar informed us, from Qatāda: he said in some readings ﴿And you take for yourselves maṣāniʿ﴾: as if you would live forever.

And Ibn Zayd used to say: "laʿallakum" in this place is interrogative.

Those who said that:

⁕ Yūnus related to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying: ﴿And you take for yourselves maṣāniʿ, that you may live forever﴾: he said: this is an interrogative, meaning: will you live forever when you build these things?

And some of the scholars of Arabic claimed that laʿallakum in this place has the meaning of "kay mā" (so that).

* *

And His saying: ﴿And when you strike, you strike as tyrants﴾

He says: and when you lash out, you lash out by killing with swords and beating with whips.

As:

⁕ al-Qāsim narrated to us, he said: al-Ḥusayn narrated to us, he said: Ḥajjāj related to me, he said: Ibn Jurayj said: ﴿And when you strike, you strike as tyrants﴾: he said: killing by sword and whip.

The exegesis of His words, ﴿This is nothing but the custom of the former peoples (137), and we are not going to be punished (138)﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: 'Ad said to their prophet Hud (ﷺ): "Your admonition to us is equal to us, as is your leaving off admonition. We will never believe you or affirm what you have brought us."'

* *

As for His words, ﴿This is nothing but the custom of the former peoples﴾:

The reciters (qurra', those who transmit the Qur'anic readings) differed over the recitation of this. The majority of the reciters of Medina, apart from Abu Ja'far, and the majority of the later reciters of Kufa, recited it as ﴿khuluq al-awwalin﴾, with a ḍammah on the kha' and the lam, meaning "the custom of those before us." Abu Ja'far and Abu 'Amr ibn al-'Ala' recited it as "in hadha illa khalq al-awwalin" with a fatḥah on the kha' and a sukun on the lam, meaning: "What you have brought us is nothing but the lies and tales of the ancients."

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil, those who explain the meaning of the Qur'an) also differed in the interpretation of this, in line with the difference of the reciters in its recitation. Some of them said: its meaning is, "This is only the religion, the customs and the morals of the ancients."

Those who said that:

* Ali related to me, saying: Abu Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiya related to me, from Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words, ﴿This is nothing but the custom of the former peoples﴾, he said: "It means the religion of the former peoples."

* Al-Hasan related to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatada, regarding His words, ﴿This is nothing but the custom of the former peoples﴾, he said: "It means this is the creation (khilqa) of the former peoples, and this is how they used to live and die."

Others said: rather, its meaning is, "This is nothing but the lies and fables of the ancients."

Those who said that:

* Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my paternal uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding ﴿This is nothing but the custom of the former peoples﴾, he said: "The fables of the ancients."

* Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, saying: 'Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Waraqa related to us, all together, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words, ﴿nothing but the custom of the former peoples﴾, he said: "Their lie."

* Al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, the same.

* Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words, ﴿This is nothing but the custom of the former peoples﴾: "This is nothing but the affair of the ancients and the fables of the ancients, which he has written down, and they are dictated to him morning and evening."

* Ibn al-Muthanna related to us, saying: Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Dawud related to us, from Amir, from Alqama, from Ibn Mas'ud, regarding ﴿This is nothing but the custom of the former peoples﴾, he said: "It means this is nothing but the fabrication (ikhtilaq) of the ancients."

* Yazid ibn Harun said: Dawud informed us, from al-Sha'bi, from Alqama, from Abdullah, that he used to recite ﴿This is nothing but the custom of the former peoples﴾ and say: "It is something they fabricated."

* Ya'qub related to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayya related to us, from Dawud, from al-Sha'bi, who said: Alqama said, regarding ﴿This is nothing but the custom of the former peoples﴾: "The fabrication of the ancients."

The most correct of the two recitations in terms of meaning is the recitation of the one who recites ﴿khuluq al-awwalin﴾ with a ḍammah on the kha' and the lam, meaning: "This is nothing but the habit and religion of the ancients," as Ibn 'Abbas said. This is because they were only rebuked for the buildings they used to erect, for their oppression of people like tyrants, and for their scant gratitude to their Lord for the blessings He had bestowed upon them. So they answered their prophet that they do what they do of that kind by imitating the practice of the nations before them and following their traces. They said: "What we are doing is nothing but the custom of the ancients," meaning by khuluq: the habit of the ancients.

What further clarifies and confirms the recitation and interpretation we have chosen is their words, ﴿and we are not going to be punished﴾. For if they did not acknowledge that they had a Lord who was able to punish them, they would not have said ﴿and we are not going to be punished﴾. Rather they would have said: "What you have brought us, O Hud, is nothing but the custom of the ancients, and we have no punisher who will punish us." But they were affirmers of the Creator, and they worshipped idols in the manner in which the idolaters of the Arabs worshipped them, saying that they would bring us near to God in closeness. Therefore they said to Hud, while denying his prophethood: ﴿It is all the same to us whether you admonish or are not among the admonishers﴾. Then they said to him: "What we are doing is nothing but the custom of those before us and their morals, and God will not punish us for it." This is as He, may His remembrance be exalted, informed us about the earlier nations before us, that they used to say to their messengers: ﴿Indeed, we found our fathers following a religion, and we are following in their footsteps﴾.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 26, verse 139–143:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So they denied him, and We destroyed them. Indeed in that is a sign, but most of them were not believers. And indeed, your Lord is the Exalted in Might, the Most Merciful.﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: The people of ʿĀd denied their messenger Hūd. The pronoun in His saying ﴿they denied him﴾ refers back to Hūd. ﴿So We destroyed them﴾ means: So We destroyed ʿĀd because of their denial of Our messenger. ﴿Indeed in that is a sign﴾ means: Indeed, in Our destruction of ʿĀd because they denied their messenger, there is a lesson and an admonition for your people, O Muhammad, who deny you regarding what you brought them from your Lord.

He says: And most of those whom We destroyed were not among those who would believe, according to Allah's foreknowledge.

﴿And indeed, your Lord is the Exalted in Might﴾ in His retribution against His enemies, ﴿the Most Merciful﴾ toward those who believe in Him.

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿The Thamūd denied the messengers. When their brother Ṣāliḥ said to them, "Will you not fear Allah? Indeed, I am to you a trustworthy messenger. So fear Allah and obey me. And I do not ask you for it any wage; my wage is only from the Lord of the worlds."﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: The Thamūd denied the messengers of Allah, when Ṣāliḥ, their brother, called them to Allah and said to them: "Will you not fear the punishment of Allah, O my people, for your disobedience to Him and your opposition to His command, by obeying the command of those who corrupt in the land of Allah?" ﴿Indeed, I am to you a messenger﴾ sent to you by Allah, to warn you of His punishment for your opposition to His command, ﴿trustworthy﴾ regarding His message which He sent with me to you. ﴿So fear Allah﴾, O people, and beware of His punishment, ﴿and obey me﴾ in my warning to you, and in the command of your Lord to follow His obedience. ﴿And I do not ask you for it any wage﴾ means: I do not ask you for any reward or recompense for my advice to you and my warning you. ﴿My wage is only from the Lord of the worlds﴾ means: My reward and recompense are only from the Lord of all that is in the heavens, all that is on the earth, and all creation between them.

The commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 26, verses 144–150:

On the interpretation (ta'wil) of His words, exalted is He: ﴿Will you be left secure in what is here, (146) among gardens and springs, (147) and crops and palm trees whose spathes are delicate (hadim)? (148) And you hew out houses from the mountains, exultantly. (149) So fear God and obey me. (150)﴾

He, exalted is His mention, says, relating the words of Salih to his people, Thamud: "Will your Lord leave you, O my people, secure in this world, fearing nothing?" ﴿Among gardens and springs﴾, meaning: among orchards and springs of water. ﴿And crops and palm trees whose spathes are delicate﴾: by the spathe (tal') he means the kufra (the sheath enclosing the flower cluster).

The people of interpretation differed concerning the meaning of His words ﴿hadim﴾ (delicate). Some of them said: its meaning is ripe and mature.

Mention of those who said this:

Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my paternal uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words ﴿and palm trees whose spathes are delicate﴾: he said, "It has ripened and reached maturity, so it is hadim."

Others said: rather, it is that which is crushed and shattered.

Mention of those who said this:

Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, saying: 'Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa' related to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿and palm trees whose spathes are delicate﴾. Muhammad ibn 'Amr said in his report: "it is crushed into shards (hashim)." Al-Harith said: "it is crushed into fragments (tahashshum)."

al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Juraij, saying: I heard 'Abd al-Karim say: I heard Mujahid say regarding His words ﴿and palm trees whose spathes are delicate﴾: "When it emerges, one grasps it and it is crushed (yahdimuhu)."

Ibn Juraij said: Mujahid said: "When it is touched, it is crushed and shatters. It is of the dates: hadim, you grasp it and it is crushed."

Others said: it is soft dates.

Mention of those who said this:

Hannad related to us, saying: Abu al-Ahwas related to us, from Simak, from 'Ikrimah regarding His words ﴿and palm trees whose spathes are delicate﴾: he said, "Hadim: soft dates."

Others said: it is when some of it rides upon other parts of it.

Mention of those who said this:

It was related to me from al-Husayn, saying: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His words ﴿its spathe is delicate﴾: "When the palm tree bears heavy fruit, parts of it ride over one another until some of it diminishes another, and then it is hadim."

The most correct of these interpretations, in my view, is to say: hadim is that which is broken because of its softness and moisture. This derives from the expression "hadama Fulan haqqahu" (so-and-so diminished his right), when he reduced it and encroached upon it. Likewise, hadm in the spathe is simply a reduction of its moisture and softness, either by the touch of hands or by parts of it riding over one another. Its origin is the passive form (maf'ul) that was turned into the form fa'il.

* *

His words: ﴿And you hew out houses from the mountains, exultantly﴾

He, exalted is His mention, says: "And you take houses from the mountains."

The readers (qurra') differed in their recitation of His words ﴿fari-hin﴾. The majority of the readers of Kufa recited it ﴿fari-hin﴾ (with alif), meaning: skilled in hewing them.

The majority of the readers of Medina and Basra recited it "fariha-in" (without alif), meaning: ostentatious and insolent (ashirin bataren).

The people of interpretation differed in their explanation of this in accordance with the difference of the readers in their recitation. Some of them said: the meaning of fari-hin is skilled.

Mention of those who said this:

Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: 'Uthham related to us, from Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, from Abu Salih and 'Abd Allah ibn Shaddad regarding ﴿and you hew out houses from the mountains, exultantly﴾: one of them said, "skilled," and the other said, "they act tyrannically."

Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim related to me, saying: Marwan related to us, saying: Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid informed us, from Abu Salih regarding ﴿and you hew out houses from the mountains, exultantly﴾: "skilled in hewing them."

'Ali related to me, saying: Abu Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiyah related to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His words ﴿fari-hin﴾: he said, "skilled."

Others said: the meaning of fari-hin is arrogant and tyrannical.

Mention of those who said this:

Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Yahya related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from al-Suddi, from 'Abd Allah ibn Shaddad regarding His words "fari-hin": he said, "they act tyrannically."

Abu Ja'far said: the correct reading is fari-hin.

Others who recited it fari-hin said: the meaning of that is clever (kaysin).

Mention of those who said this:

It was related from al-Husayn, saying: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His words ﴿fari-hin﴾: "clever."

Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Yahya ibn Wadih related to us, saying: 'Ubayd related to us, from al-Dahhak, that he recited ﴿fari-hin﴾ and said: "clever."

Others said: fari-hin means ostentatious.

Mention of those who said this:

Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my paternal uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His words ﴿And you hew out houses from the mountains, exultantly﴾: he said, "ostentatious," and it is said, "clever."

Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, saying: 'Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa' related to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid regarding His words "bayutan fari-hin" (houses, exultantly): he said, "ostentatious (shirhin)."

al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Juraij, from Mujahid, similarly.

Others said: the meaning of that is strong.

Mention of those who said this:

Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His words "And you hew out houses from the mountains, exultantly": "al-farah: the strong."

Others said regarding this:

al-Hasan related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah regarding His words "fari-hin": he said, "admiring of your handiwork."

The correct view on this matter is to say: the recitation of the one who recited ﴿fari-hin﴾ and the recitation of the one who recited "fari-hin" are two well-known readings, widely transmitted among the scholars of recitation, and whichever of the two a reader recites, he is correct. The meaning of the recitation of the one who recited ﴿fari-hin﴾ is: skilled in hewing them, choosing the places for their hewing, clever, from al-firah (skill). The meaning of the recitation of the one who recited "fari-hin" is: exulting and insolent. It may also be that the meaning of fari and fari-h is one, so that fari is formed on its own pattern, its origin being from the form fa'ala yaf'alu, and fari-h is an attribute, just as it is said: "so-and-so is skilled in this matter" (hadhaqa). Among the uses of fari meaning exultant is the verse of the poet 'Adi ibn Wada' al-'Awfi from the Azd:

I do not yield when a crisis grips me,
and you will never see me with a joyful (fari-h) pursuit of goods.

His words: ﴿So fear God and obey me﴾

He, exalted is His mention, says: "So fear the punishment of God, O people, for your disobedience to your Lord and your opposition to His command, and obey me in my advice to you and my warning to you of God's punishment, that you may be rightly guided."

The commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 26, verses 144–150:

On the interpretation (ta'wil) of His words, exalted is He: ﴿Will you be left secure in what is here, (146) among gardens and springs, (147) and crops and palm trees whose spathes are delicate (hadim)? (148) And you hew out houses from the mountains, exultantly. (149) So fear God and obey me. (150)﴾

He, exalted is His mention, says, relating the words of Salih to his people, Thamud: "Will your Lord leave you, O my people, secure in this world, fearing nothing?" ﴿Among gardens and springs﴾, meaning: among orchards and springs of water. ﴿And crops and palm trees whose spathes are delicate﴾: by the spathe (tal') he means the kufra (the sheath enclosing the flower cluster).

The people of interpretation differed concerning the meaning of His words ﴿hadim﴾ (delicate). Some of them said: its meaning is ripe and mature.

Mention of those who said this:

Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my paternal uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words ﴿and palm trees whose spathes are delicate﴾: he said, "It has ripened and reached maturity, so it is hadim."

Others said: rather, it is that which is crushed and shattered.

Mention of those who said this:

Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, saying: 'Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa' related to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿and palm trees whose spathes are delicate﴾. Muhammad ibn 'Amr said in his report: "it is crushed into shards (hashim)." Al-Harith said: "it is crushed into fragments (tahashshum)."

al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Juraij, saying: I heard 'Abd al-Karim say: I heard Mujahid say regarding His words ﴿and palm trees whose spathes are delicate﴾: "When it emerges, one grasps it and it is crushed (yahdimuhu)."

Ibn Juraij said: Mujahid said: "When it is touched, it is crushed and shatters. It is of the dates: hadim, you grasp it and it is crushed."

Others said: it is soft dates.

Mention of those who said this:

Hannad related to us, saying: Abu al-Ahwas related to us, from Simak, from 'Ikrimah regarding His words ﴿and palm trees whose spathes are delicate﴾: he said, "Hadim: soft dates."

Others said: it is when some of it rides upon other parts of it.

Mention of those who said this:

It was related to me from al-Husayn, saying: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His words ﴿its spathe is delicate﴾: "When the palm tree bears heavy fruit, parts of it ride over one another until some of it diminishes another, and then it is hadim."

The most correct of these interpretations, in my view, is to say: hadim is that which is broken because of its softness and moisture. This derives from the expression "hadama Fulan haqqahu" (so-and-so diminished his right), when he reduced it and encroached upon it. Likewise, hadm in the spathe is simply a reduction of its moisture and softness, either by the touch of hands or by parts of it riding over one another. Its origin is the passive form (maf'ul) that was turned into the form fa'il.

The interpretation of the words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And do not obey the command of those who commit excess, who spread corruption in the land and do not reform﴾ [26:151-152] ﴿They said, "You are only of those bewitched."﴾ [26:153]

His saying, may His remembrance be exalted, reporting the words of Salih to his people from Thamud: "Do not obey, O people, the command of those who are excessive against themselves in their persistence in disobeying Allah and their audacity toward His wrath. They were the nine men who used to spread corruption in the land and not reform, from Thamud, whom Allah, may His praise be exalted, described with His saying: ﴿And there were in the city nine men who spread corruption in the land and did not reform﴾ [27:48]." He means: those who strive in the land of Allah with His disobedience and do not reform, meaning: and do not reform themselves by acting in obedience to Allah.

And His saying: ﴿You are only of those bewitched (al-musahharin)﴾

The people of interpretation differed regarding its meaning. Some of them said: its meaning is "You are only of the bewitched (al-mashurin)."

Mention of those who said that:

Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿You are only of those bewitched﴾: "of the bewitched."

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, the same.

Al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Mamar informed us, from Qatada, regarding His saying: ﴿You are only of those bewitched﴾: "You are only of the bewitched."

Others said: its meaning is "of the created beings."

Mention of those who said that:

Muhammad ibn Ubayd narrated to me, saying: Musa ibn Amr narrated to us, from Abu Salih, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿You are only of those bewitched﴾: "of the created beings."

The people knowledgeable in the speech of the Arabs differed regarding the meaning of this. Some of the scholars of Basra said: every one who eats, whether human or animal, is musahhar, because he has a sahr (the lower part of the stomach or the time before dawn) in which what he eats is nourished. He cited as evidence the verse of Labid:

"If you ask us what we are doing, indeed we are sparrows among this created kind that is nourished (al-musahhar)."

[The commentary notes on this verse: Abu Ubayda cited it in Majaz al-Qur'an, and in Lisan al-Arab the root s-h-r is explained as: sahharahu bi'l-ta'am, meaning he nourished him with food and drink; and it is said: he deceived him. Al-sahr means nourishment. Imru' al-Qays said: "We are hastening toward an unseen matter, and we are nourished with food and drink." (154) He said, "This is a she-camel; she has a share of water, and you have a share of water on a known day." He, the Exalted, says, relating the words of Thamud to their prophet Salih: "You are only a human being like us," from the children of Adam, who eats what we eat and drinks what we drink; you are not a lord or an angel, so why should we follow you? * *

Al-Tabari also narrated to us, citing Ahmad ibn Amr al-Basri, who said: Amr ibn Asim al-Kilabi related to us, who said: Dawud ibn Abi al-Furat related to us, who said: Ulba' ibn Ahmar related to us, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, that Salih, the Prophet (ﷺ), was sent by God to his people. They believed in him and followed him, but then Salih died, and they turned back from Islam. Salih came to them and said to them: "I am Salih." They said: "If you are truthful, bring us a sign." As for His words: "He said, 'This is a she-camel; she has a share of water, and you have a share of water on a known day.'"

The word "shurb" (share) means the portion and allotment of water; one says: she has a portion of water and you have the like of it. The forms shurb, shirb and shrub are all verbal nouns, with the vowel pronounced in each case as a u, a, or i.

It has been related from the Arabs by hearing that "its last is the least of them in shurb and shirb" (drinking share).

He says: do not touch her with anything that would harm her, such as hamstringing, killing, or the like.

**The Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami' al-Bayan) on Surah 26, Verses 165–168**

**On the interpretation (ta'wil) of His words:** ﴿Do you approach the males among the worlds? (165) And leave what your Lord has created for you of your spouses? Rather, you are a people transgressing.﴾ (166)

Its meaning, by His words ﴿Do you approach the males among the worlds?﴾: Do you marry males from among the children of Adam by way of their posteriors?

* *

As for His words ﴿and leave what your Lord has created for you of your spouses﴾:

He says: and you abandon what your Lord has created for you of your spouses, from their private parts, which He made lawful for you. It has been reported that in the reading of Abdullah (Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him) it is: "وَتَذَرُونَ ما أصْلَحَ لَكُمْ رَبُّكُمْ مِنْ أزْوَاجِكُمْ" (and leave what your Lord has made good for you of your spouses).

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 26, verses 169–175:

The interpretation (ta'wil) of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿My Lord, deliver me and my family from what they do﴾ (169) ﴿So We delivered him and his family, all of them,﴾ (170) ﴿except an old woman among those who remained behind﴾ (171).

His saying, may His remembrance be exalted: Lot cried out for help when his people threatened him with expulsion from their city if he did not desist from forbidding them from committing lewdness. So he said, ﴿My Lord, deliver me and my family﴾ from Your punishment of them for what they do of mounting males. ﴿So We delivered him and his family﴾ from Our punishment with which We punished the people of Lot, ﴿all of them, except an old woman among those who remained behind﴾, meaning among those who stayed behind, because of the long passage of years upon her, so she became decrepit. She was destroyed from among the family of Lot, because she used to direct her people to the guests.

It has also been said that she was described as among those who remained behind only because she was not destroyed together with her people in their town, and that the stone only struck her after she had left their town with Lot and his two daughters. Thus she was among those who remained behind after her people, and then Allah destroyed her with what He rained upon the remnants of the people of Lot of stones. We have already explained this earlier, with its proofs that make repeating it unnecessary.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 26, verse 176–179:

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, words: ﴿Then We destroyed the others. And We rained upon them a rain, and evil was the rain of those who were warned. Indeed, in that is a sign, but most of them were not believers. And indeed, your Lord is the Exalted in Might, the Merciful﴾

He, may He be exalted, says: Then We destroyed the others, the people of Lot, by annihilation. ﴿And We rained upon them a rain﴾ means that Allah sent down upon them stones of sijjil from the sky. ﴿And evil was the rain of those who were warned﴾ means: evil was that rain, the rain of the people whom their prophet warned but who denied him. ﴿Indeed, in that is a sign﴾ means: He, may He be exalted, says: indeed, in Our destruction of the people of Lot with the destruction we have described, for their denial of Our messenger, there is a lesson and an admonition for your people, O Muhammad, by which they may take heed in their denial of you and their rejection of the truth that you brought them from your Lord. ﴿But most of them were not believers﴾ in the prior knowledge of Allah. ﴿And indeed, your Lord is the Exalted in Might, the Merciful﴾ toward those who believed in Him.

* *

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, words: ﴿The companions of the Thicket denied the messengers. When Shu'ayb said to them, "Will you not fear Allah? Indeed, I am to you a trustworthy messenger. So fear Allah and obey me."﴾

He, may He be exalted, says: ﴿The companions of the Thicket denied﴾. Al-Ayka: dense, intertwined trees; it is the singular of al-ayk, and any dense tree is called ayka by the Arabs. Among the examples is the verse of Nabigha of the Banu Dhubyan:

"She reveals, with the two primary feathers of a dove of the thicket, a hail whose gums are tinged with kohl."

[[The verse is by al-Nabigha al-Dhubyani, Ziyad ibn Mu'awiya (Mukhtar al-Shi'r al-Jahili, with the commentary of Mustafa al-Saqqa, Halabi edition, p. 185). Its commentator said: "tajlu" means "reveals." Al-qawadim are the front feathers of a bird's wing, which are very black; he likened the blackness of her lips to the primary feathers, and the whiteness of her teeth to the whiteness of hail. Al-lithath are the sockets of the teeth; among their customs was to sprinkle kohl on them to show the whiteness of the teeth. End of quote. Al-ayka: thick, intertwined trees. It was said: it is a thicket that grows lote-trees, arak and similar tender trees. Some restricted it to the growing place and gathering of the athil tree. Abu Hanifa al-Dinawari said: al-ayka may also be a group of trees, even of palms. He said: the first meaning is better known. The plural is ayk.]]

The companions of the Thicket were the people of Madyan, as has been mentioned.

Mention of those who said this:

* Ali related to me, he said: Abu Salih narrated to us, he said: Mu'awiya related to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿The companions of the Thicket denied the messengers﴾, he said: the companions of the thicket (ghayda).

* Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, he said: my father related to me, he said: my paternal uncle related to me, he said: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿The companions of the Thicket denied the messengers﴾, he said: al-Ayka is the gathering of trees.

* al-Qasim related to us, he said: al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Ibn Abbas said, regarding His words: ﴿The companions of the Thicket denied the messengers﴾: they are the people of Madyan, and al-Ayka is the dense trees.

* Yunus related to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words: ﴿The companions of the Thicket denied the messengers﴾: al-Ayka is the trees. Allah sent Shu'ayb to his people from the people of Madyan and to the people of the desert. He said: they are the companions of Layka, and Layka and al-Ayka are one and the same.

* *

As for His words: ﴿When Shu'ayb said to them, "Will you not fear Allah?"﴾

He, may He be exalted, says: Shu'ayb said to them: Will you not fear the punishment of Allah for your disobedience to your Lord? ﴿Indeed, I am to you a messenger from Allah, trustworthy﴾ in His revelation. ﴿So fear﴾ the punishment of ﴿Allah﴾ for your opposition to His command, ﴿and obey me﴾ so that you may be guided.

* *

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 26, verses 184–187:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And fear Him who created you and the generations of the former peoples (al-jibillah al-awwalin)﴾ [184] ﴿They said, "You are only of those bewitched."﴾ [185] ﴿You are not but a human being like us, and indeed we think you are of the liars.﴾ [186] ﴿So cause a piece of the sky to fall upon us, if you should be of the truthful.﴾ [187]

His exalted mention says: ﴿And fear﴾, O people, the punishment of your Lord ﴿who created you and created the former generations (al-jibillah al-awwalin)﴾. He means by al-jibillah: the earlier creations. Concerning al-jibillah, the Arabs have two dialectal forms: with a kasra on the jim and the ba' and a shaddah on the lam, and with a damma on the jim and the ba' and a shaddah on the lam. When the ha' is removed from its end, the damma on the jim and the ba' is more common, as the One whose praise is exalted said: "And he had already led astray from you a great multitude (jibillan kathiran)." Sometimes they also pronounce the ba' of al-jabl with a sukun, as Abu Dhu'ayb said:

Death-fates that bring near the ruin upon its people
openly, and they enjoy the human multitude (al-anas al-jibl) [[The verse is by Abu Dhu'ayb al-Hudhali (Lisan: jabal). "Manaya" is plural of "maniyyah," meaning death. "Huttuf" is plural of "hatf," meaning destruction. "Al-anas" means people. "Al-jabl" means a community of creation. It has variant forms: the jim may take three vowels, with a sukun on the ba'; it may also be pronounced with a damma on the jim and the ba', with a shaddah on the lam. The Lisan says: "Wahy jabal kathir." Abu Dhu'ayb said: "Manaya..." the verse, i.e., many. He means: all people are enjoyment for death, by which it enjoys them. Ibn Barri said: it is also transmitted as "al-jubl," with a damma on the jim; he said Abu 'Ubaydah also transmitted it so. The saying of God, mighty and majestic: "And he had already led astray from you a great multitude (jibillan kathiran)" is read: jibillan (with a damma and sukun) according to Abu 'Amr; jubulan (with two dammas) according to al-Kisa'i; jibilan (with a kasra and sukun) according to al-A'raj and Isa ibn 'Umar; jibillan (with two kasras and a shaddah on the lam) according to the people of Madina; jubbulan (with two dammas and shaddah) according to al-Hasan and Ibn Abi Ishaq. He said: it is also permissible to read jibal (with a kasra then fatha), plural of jibillah (with a kasra and sukun), and in all of these forms it means: a great number of creatures.]]

Concerning the meaning of al-jibillah, the people of interpretation have said something similar to what we have said.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 26, verses 188–189:

The explanation of His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿He said, "My Lord is most knowing of what you do." (188) So they denied him, and the punishment of the Day of the Shade seized them. Indeed, it was the punishment of a tremendous day.﴾ (189)

The Exalted says: Shu'ayb said to his people, ﴿"My Lord is most knowing of what you do"﴾, meaning: He encompasses their deeds, nothing of them is hidden from Him, and He will recompense them for them. ﴿So they denied him﴾, meaning: his people denied him. ﴿So the punishment of the Day of the Shade seized them﴾. By "the Shade" is meant a cloud that shaded them. When they gathered beneath it, it burst into fire upon them and burned them, and the reports came with this.

Mention of those who said this:

• Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from Abu Ishaq, from Zayd ibn Mu'awiyah, concerning His saying: ﴿So the punishment of the Day of the Shade seized them﴾, he said: A heat afflicted them that disturbed them in their houses, so a cloud arose for them like a shade, and they hastened to it. When they gathered beneath it, the quaking seized them.

• Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Ya'qub related to us, from Ja'far, concerning His saying: ﴿the punishment of the Day of the Shade﴾, he said: They used to dig tunnels to cool themselves in them, but when they entered them they found them hotter than the outside, and the shade was a cloud.

• Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Jarir ibn Hazim related to me that he heard Qatadah say: Shu'ayb was sent to two communities: to his people, the people of Madyan, and to the companions of the Thicket (al-Aykah). The Aykah was of dense trees. When God wished to punish them, God sent upon them an intense heat, and He raised for them the punishment like a cloud. When it drew near them, they went out toward it, hoping for its coolness, and when they were beneath it, it rained fire upon them. He said: That is His saying: ﴿So the punishment of the Day of the Shade seized them﴾.

• Al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Sa'id ibn Zayd, brother of Hammad ibn Zayd, related to me, saying: Hatim ibn Abi Saghirah related to us, saying: Yazid al-Bahili related to me, saying: I asked 'Abdullah ibn 'Abbas about this verse: ﴿So the punishment of the Day of the Shade seized them. Indeed, it was the punishment of a tremendous day﴾. 'Abdullah ibn 'Abbas said: God sent upon them a sultry wind and intense heat, which seized their breaths. So they entered the houses, but the inner parts of the houses seized their breaths, so they came out of the houses fleeing [[Harab: perhaps a plural of harib; I have not found it in Lisan al-Arab.]] into the desert. God then sent a cloud which shaded them from the sun, and they found in it coolness and pleasure. Some of them called to others until, when they gathered beneath it, God sent it upon them as fire. 'Abdullah ibn 'Abbas said: That is the punishment of the Day of the Shade, ﴿Indeed, it was the punishment of a tremendous day﴾.

• Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, saying: 'Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa' related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning His saying: "the Day of the Shade": he said: the shading of the punishment over them.

• al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid: ﴿the punishment of the Day of the Shade﴾, he said: The punishment shaded the people of Shu'ayb.

Ibn Jurayj said: When God sent down the first of the punishment upon them, an intense heat seized them, so God raised for them a cloud. A group of them went out toward it to seek shade beneath it, and there reached them from it refreshment, coolness and a pleasant breeze. Then God poured upon them from above them, from that cloud, a punishment. That is His saying: ﴿the punishment of the Day of the Shade﴾.

• al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Abu Sufyan related to us, from Ma'mar ibn Rashid, saying: A man from our companions related to me, from some scholars, who said: They had abandoned a prescribed penalty, so God expanded their provision; then they abandoned another prescribed penalty, and God expanded their provision; then they abandoned another, and God expanded their provision. Whenever they abandoned a prescribed penalty, God expanded their provision, until, when He willed to destroy them, God set upon them a heat they could not endure, and neither shade nor water benefited them, until one of them departed and sought shelter beneath a shade, and found coolness there. He called out to his companions: "Come to the coolness!" They hastened to it, until, when they had gathered, God set it ablaze upon them with fire. That is the punishment of the Day of the Shade.

• al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Abu Tumaylah related to us, from Abu Hamzah, from Jabir, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: Whoever from the scholars tells you what the punishment of the Day of the Shade is, then deny him.

• It was related from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say concerning His saying: ﴿So the punishment of the Day of the Shade seized them﴾: the people of Shu'ayb. God withheld from them the shade and the wind, so an intense heat afflicted them. Then God sent them a cloud in which was the punishment. When they saw the cloud, they set off heading for it, supposing they would find shade, and it blazed upon them as fire and destroyed them.

• Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His saying: ﴿So the punishment of the Day of the Shade seized them. Indeed, it was the punishment of a tremendous day﴾: God sent to them a shading cloud, and He sent to the sun, which burned whatever was on the face of the earth. So they all went out to that shade, and when they had all gathered, God uncovered the shade from them and heated the sun upon them, so they burned as locusts burn in a frying pan.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Indeed, it was the punishment of a tremendous day﴾

The Exalted says: Indeed, the punishment of the Day of the Shade was the punishment of a tremendous day for the people of Shu'ayb.
