Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 26, verses 190–195:

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿Indeed in that is a sign, but most of them were not believers (190). And indeed, your Lord is the Exalted in Might, the Merciful (191).﴾

He, the Exalted, says: Indeed, in Our punishment of the people of Shu'ayb, by the Day of the Shade, because they denied their prophet Shu'ayb, is a sign for your people, O Muhammad, and a lesson for whoever takes heed, if they take heed that Our practice towards them, by their denial of you, is Our practice towards the companions of the Thicket. ﴿But most of them were not believers﴾ in Our prior knowledge concerning them. ﴿And indeed, your Lord﴾ O Muhammad ﴿is the Exalted in Might﴾ in His vengeance, against whomever He takes vengeance upon of His enemies, ﴿the Merciful﴾ toward whoever of His creatures repents and turns back to His obedience.

* *

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿And indeed, it is a revelation from the Lord of the worlds (192). The Trustworthy Spirit has brought it down (193) upon your heart, that you may be among the warners (194) in a clear Arabic tongue (195).﴾

He, the Exalted, says: And indeed, this Qur'an is ﴿a revelation from the Lord of the worlds﴾. The pronoun in His words ﴿And indeed, it﴾ refers back to the Reminder mentioned in His words: ﴿No reminder comes to them from the Most Merciful﴾.

The people of interpretation have said things similar to what we have said about this.

Those who said so:

⁕ Al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, regarding His words: ﴿a revelation from the Lord of the worlds﴾, he said: This is the Qur'an.

The reciters differed over the recitation of His words ﴿The Trustworthy Spirit has brought it down﴾. The reciters of most of the Hijaz and Basra read ﴿nazala﴾ (with the verb unvoweled-doubling-free, i.e., lightened) with ﴿al-Ruh al-Amin﴾ in the nominative case, meaning: the Trustworthy Spirit is the one who brought the Qur'an down upon Muhammad, and he is Jibril. The reciters of most of Kufa read it ﴿nuzzila﴾ (with the zay doubled) with ﴿al-Ruh al-Amin﴾ in the accusative case, meaning: the Lord of the worlds brought down the Qur'an by the Trustworthy Spirit, and he is Jibril, peace be upon him.

The correct view in this matter, in our opinion, is to say: they are two widely transmitted recitations among the reciters of the regions, close in meaning. Whichever one the reciter reads is correct, because when the Trustworthy Spirit descended upon Muhammad with the Qur'an, he did not descend with it except by God's command to him to descend, and no one who believes in God would be ignorant that this is so, and that when God sends it down with him, it descends.

The people of interpretation have said things similar to what we have said, that the one meant by the Trustworthy Spirit in this place is Jibril.

Those who said so:

⁕ Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿The Trustworthy Spirit has brought it down﴾, he said: Jibril.

⁕ Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, regarding the words of God: ﴿The Trustworthy Spirit has brought it down﴾, he said: Jibril.

⁕ Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: ﴿al-Ruh al-Amin﴾ is Jibril.

⁕ I was told by al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His words: ﴿al-Ruh al-Amin﴾, he said: Jibril.

* *

As for His words ﴿upon your heart﴾:

He says: The Trustworthy Spirit brought it down and recited it to you, O Muhammad, until you retained it in your heart.

* *

As for His words: ﴿that you may be among the warners﴾:

He says: that you may be among the messengers of God who used to warn those to whom they were sent from among their peoples, so that you warn your people who deny the signs of God through this revelation.

* *

As for His words: ﴿in a clear Arabic tongue﴾:

He says: that you may warn your people in a clear Arabic tongue, which makes clear to whoever hears it that it is Arabic; and it was revealed in the tongue of the Arabs. The preposition "bi" in His words ﴿bi-lisan﴾ is connected to His words ﴿nazala﴾. He, the Exalted, mentioned here that this Qur'an was revealed in a clear Arabic tongue only to inform the idolaters of Quraysh that He sent it down in this way, lest they say that it was revealed in other than our tongue, so we turn away from it and do not listen to it because we do not understand it. This is in fact a rebuke to them. For He, the Exalted, said: ﴿No new reminder comes to them from the Most Merciful except that they turn away from it﴾. Then He said: They did not turn away from it because they do not understand its meanings; rather they understand them, since it is the revelation of the Lord of the worlds, brought down by the Trustworthy Spirit in their Arabic tongue. But they turned away from it out of denial and arrogance: ﴿So they have denied, and there will come to them the news of that which they used to mock﴾. Just as there came to those nations whose stories We have related in this surah, when they denied their messengers, the news of that which they used to deny.

And His words: ﴿They will not believe in it until they see the painful punishment﴾

He says: We did that to them so that they would not believe in this Qur'an until they see the painful punishment in the immediate life of this world, as the nations whose stories Allah related in this surah saw it. His words "They will not believe" are in the nominative because the Arabs, when they place "la" (not) in a position like this one, sometimes apocopate what follows it [i.e. jussive], and sometimes they use the nominative, saying: "I tied the horse, lest it break loose (la tanfalit)," and "I tightened the knot, lest it come undone (la yanhalla)," both in the jussive and nominative. They do this because the interpretation of that is: "If I do not tighten the knot, it will come undone." So its jussive form is based on the interpretation, and its nominative form is because the jussive particle is not apparent.

Among the evidence for the jussive in this is the poet's saying:

"If you had, when you came to us, tried to see us, or come to us on foot, the horse would not know [you]." [[This line is among the evidences of al-Farra' in Ma'ani al-Qur'an (manuscript of the al-Jami'ah photocopy, folio 230). He said: His words "Thus We made it enter" — you say: We made disbelief enter into the hearts of the criminals "so that they would not believe in it until they see the painful punishment." When the position of kay (so that) in such a case is both "la" and "in" together, the jussive with "la" and the nominative are both correct. The Arabs say: "I tied the horse, lest it break loose," in both the jussive and nominative; and "I bound the slave, lest he flee," in both jussive and nominative. It is jussive because its interpretation is: "If I do not tie it, it will flee"; so it is jussive by way of interpretation. One of the Banu 'Uqayl recited to me: "Until we saw the best of deeds among us, a silence that evil does not separate, a separator" — recited with both nominative and jussive. Another said: "If you had, when you came to us..." with both nominative and jussive. His saying: "Lo, you have long kept her from drinking..." is the evidence that follows this.]]

"Indeed you have long kept her from drinking, so she does not drink; so leave her, and let the buckets and the water-draw be cooled."
[[The line is in Lisan al-'Arab (root h-l-')]. Its transmission is "qad taalama" etc. He said: he drove the camels and cattle away from water, preventing them from coming to drink, and likewise a people kept others away from water. Ibn al-A'rabi said: A Qurayb said: There was a man in love with a woman, and he married her; then the women came to her, and some of them said to others: "Indeed you have long kept her from water, so she does not come." The verse is evidence like the previous one, that "la tarid" permits both nominative and jussive by the interpretation that al-Farra' mentioned.]]

And His words: ﴿and he had recited it to them﴾

Then He said, making him despair of their belief and [declaring] that they are destined for destruction by some of His punishments, as some of the nations whose stories He related in this surah were destroyed. "And if We had sent it down upon some of the non-Arabs, O Muhammad, it would not be your concern, for you are a man among them, and they would say to you: 'You are only a human like us; why was an angel not sent down with him?' Then that non-Arab would have recited this Qur'an to them, and they would have had no excuse by which to repel that it is the truth and that it is a revelation from Me; they would not have been believers in it." So lessen your eagerness for their belief. Then He, exalted is His remembrance, emphasized the report of what has been decreed upon these polytheists, whom He made His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ despair of believing, of wretchedness and affliction. He said: just as We have decreed upon these that they will not believe in this Qur'an, ﴿And if We had sent it down upon some of the non-Arabs, and he had recited it to them, thus We made it enter﴾ disbelief and rejection ﴿into the hearts of the criminals﴾. The pronoun in His words "We made it enter" refers back to His words "they would not have been believers in it," as if He said: thus We caused to enter into the hearts of the criminals the abandonment of belief in this Qur'an.

* *

And His words: ﴿and he had recited it to them﴾

"And time with man is dawwari [turning]."

"I wept, and the one who wept much wept; and youth only comes to the young...
Did it delight you, while you are an old man? And time with man is dawwari...
It has consumed the generations and it is qa'sari; and with cunning the one who is cunning is deceived."

He says: I wept, and by wisdom your weeping was [appropriate]. al-Qansari: the aged and ancient. dawwari: revolving, i.e. it turns a person and turns him through stages and states. al-Qa'sari: the strong, meaning time. The point of evidence is in his saying "dawwari." In Lisan al-'Arab it says: "i.e. revolving with him," with the attribution of a thing to itself (i.e. its attribution to itself, since dawwari is attributed to dawwar, so the word of the attributed-to is like the word of the attribution). This is when it occurs as an occurrence that cannot be rejected. End.]]

Its meaning is dawwar, so he attributed it to the action of itself.

Its plural with waw and nun is: ahmari and ahmarun, a'jami and a'jamun, on the pattern of ash'athi and ash'athin, and ash'ari and ash'arin; and upon this is His saying, mighty and majestic: "And if We had sent it down upon some of the non-Arabs."]]

As for when it is intended to attribute a man to his origin among the 'ajam, and not to describe him as not eloquent in speech, one says: "This is a man 'ajami, and these are two men 'ajamiyan, and these are people 'ajam," just as one says: "'arabi, and 'arabiyan, and people 'arab." When one says "This is a man a'jami," he is attributed to himself, as one says of a red man: "This is a big ahmari," and as al-Ajjaj said:

"And time with man is dawwari [turning]."

[[This is a verse from the rajaz meter by al-'Ajjaj, the well-known rajaz poet (Lisan al-'Arab, root dwr; Arajiz al-'Arab by al-Sayyid Tawfiq al-Bakri, p. 174). It is from a sorrowful urjuzah of his, which begins:

"I wept, and the one who wept much wept; and youth only comes to the young...
Did it delight you, while you are an old man? And time with man is dawwari...
It has consumed the generations and it is qa'sari; and with cunning the one who is cunning is deceived."

He says: I wept, and by wisdom your weeping was [appropriate]. al-Qansari: the aged and ancient. dawwari: revolving, i.e. it turns a person and turns him through stages and states. al-Qa'sari: the strong, meaning time. The point of evidence is in his saying "dawwari." In Lisan al-'Arab it says: "i.e. revolving with him," with the attribution of a thing to itself (i.e. its attribution to itself, since dawwari is attributed to dawwar, so the word of the attributed-to is like the word of the attribution). Ibn Sidah said: this is the view of the lexicographers. al-Farisi said: it is on the form of the nisbah (attributive form), but it is not a true nisbah; its parallels are bakhti and kursi. In Lisan al-'Arab (root 'jm): the a'jam is attributed to one who has 'ujmah in his tongue, so one says "a non-Arabic tongue" and "a non-Arabic book," but one does not say "a non-Arab man" meaning he is attributed to himself, unless a'jam and a'jami have the same meaning, like dawwar and dawwari, and jamal qa'sar and qa'sari. This is when it occurs as an occurrence that cannot be rejected. End.]]

Its meaning is dawwar, so he attributed it to the action of itself.

Those of the people of ta'wil (interpretation) said something similar to what we have said regarding that.

Those who said that:

- Ibn al-Muthanna related to us, saying: 'Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Dawud related to us, from Muhammad ibn Abi Musa, who said: I was standing beside 'Abd Allah ibn Mut'i at 'Arafah, and he recited this verse: ﴿And if We had sent it down upon some of the non-Arabs, and he had recited it to them, they would not have been believers in it﴾ He said: If it had been sent down upon this camel of mine and it spoke it, they would not have believed in it, ﴿they would have said: "Why have its verses not been made clear?"﴾ until an Arab and a non-Arab understand it, if we had done that.

- Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Ibn Idris related to us, saying: I heard Dawud ibn Abi Hind, from Muhammad ibn Abi Musa, who said: 'Abd Allah ibn Mut'i was standing at 'Arafah, and he recited this verse: ﴿And if We had sent it down upon some of the non-Arabs, and he had recited it to them, they would not have been believers in it﴾ He said: He said: "This camel of mine is a'jam; if it were sent down upon this one, they would not have been believers in it."

It has been related from Qatadah concerning that:

- al-Hasan related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah: ﴿And if We had sent it down upon some of the non-Arabs﴾ He said: If Allah had sent it down as non-Arabic, they would have been the most wretched of people regarding it, because they would not recognize it in the non-Arabic language.

What we have mentioned from Qatadah is an opinion with no basis, because he directed the speech to mean: "If We had sent it down as non-Arabic." But the revelation is: ﴿And if We had sent it down upon some of the non-Arabs﴾, meaning: if We had sent down this Arabic Qur'an upon an animal of the non-Arabs, or upon some of what does not speak clearly; and He did not say: "If We had sent it down as non-Arabic." So the meaning of the speech is what he [Ibn Mut'i] said.

* *

And His words: ﴿and he had recited it to them﴾

He says: and he recited this Qur'an to the disbelievers of your people, O Muhammad, those upon whom I have decreed that they will not believe, that non-Arab [i.e. the messenger] they would not have been believers in it. He means: they would not have believed in it, because of the wretchedness that has already occurred to them in My foreknowledge. This is consolation from Allah to His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ regarding his people, lest his grief become intense at their turning away from him and their aversion to listening to this Qur'an, for he ﷺ was intensely eager for their acceptance of him and their entering into what he invited them to, until his Lord rebuked him for the intensity of his eagerness for that from them, and said to him: ﴿Perhaps you would kill yourself with grief that they do not become believers﴾ [26:3]. Then He said, making him despair of their belief and [declaring] that they are destined for destruction by some of His punishments, as some of the nations whose stories He related in this surah were destroyed. "And if We had sent it down upon some of the non-Arabs, O Muhammad, it would not be your concern, for you are a man among them, and they would say to you: 'You are only a human like us; why was an angel not sent down with him?' Then that non-Arab would have recited this Qur'an to them, and they would have had no excuse by which to repel that it is the truth and that it is a revelation from Me; they would not have been believers in it." So lessen your eagerness for their belief. Then He, exalted is His remembrance, emphasized the report of what has been decreed upon these polytheists, whom He made His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ despair of believing, of wretchedness and affliction. He said: just as We have decreed upon these that they will not believe in this Qur'an, ﴿And if We had sent it down upon some of the non-Arabs, and he had recited it to them, thus We made it enter﴾ disbelief and rejection ﴿into the hearts of the criminals﴾. By His words "We made it enter" He means: We caused to enter. The pronoun in His words "We made it enter" refers back to His words "they would not have been believers in it," as if He said: thus We caused to enter into the hearts of the criminals the abandonment of belief in this Qur'an.

Those of the people of ta'wil said something similar to what we have said in the interpretation of that.

Those who said that:

- al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Juraij, regarding His words: ﴿Thus We made it enter﴾ He said: disbelief ﴿into the hearts of the criminals﴾.

- Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words: ﴿Thus We made it enter into the hearts of the criminals. They will not believe in it until they see the painful punishment﴾. [[The omission in Ibn Zayd's tafsir of what he intended from the verse; perhaps it is disbelief, or polytheism, or something similar, or the like.]]

- 'Ali ibn Sahl related to me, saying: Zayd ibn Abi al-Zarqa' related to us, from Sufyan, from Humayd, from al-Hasan, regarding this verse: ﴿Thus We made it enter into the hearts of the criminals﴾ He said: We created it.

- He said: Zayd related to us, from Hammad ibn Salamah, from Humayd, who said: I asked al-Hasan in the house of Abu Khalifah about His words: ﴿Thus We made it enter into the hearts of the criminals﴾ He said: Shirk [polytheism], He made it enter their hearts.

* *

And His words: ﴿They will not believe in it until they see the painful punishment﴾

He says: We did that to them so that they would not believe in this Qur'an until they see the painful punishment in the immediate life of this world, as the nations whose stories Allah related in this surah saw it. His words "They will not believe" are in the nominative because the Arabs, when they place "la" (not) in a position like this one, sometimes apocopate what follows it [i.e. jussive], and sometimes they use the nominative, saying: "I tied the horse, lest it break loose (la tanfalit)," and "I tightened the knot, lest it come undone (la yanhalla)," both in the jussive and nominative. They do this because the interpretation of that is: "If I do not tighten the knot, it will come undone." So its jussive form is based on the interpretation, and its nominative form is because the jussive particle is not apparent.

Among the evidence for the jussive in this is the poet's saying:

"If you had, when you came to us, tried to see us, or come to us on foot, the horse would not know [you]." [[This line is among the evidences of al-Farra' in Ma'ani al-Qur'an (manuscript of the al-Jami'ah photocopy, folio 230). He said: His words "Thus We made it enter" — you say: We made disbelief enter into the hearts of the criminals "so that they would not believe in it until they see the painful punishment." When the position of kay (so that) in such a case is both "la" and "in" together, the jussive with "la" and the nominative are both correct. The Arabs say: "I tied the horse, lest it break loose," in both the jussive and nominative; and "I bound the slave, lest he flee," in both jussive and nominative. It is jussive because its interpretation is: "If I do not tie it, it will flee"; so it is jussive by way of interpretation. One of the Banu 'Uqayl recited to me: "Until we saw the best of deeds among us, a silence that evil does not separate, a separator" — recited with both nominative and jussive. Another said: "If you had, when you came to us..." with both nominative and jussive. His saying: "Lo, you have long kept her from drinking..." is the evidence that follows this.]]

And another's saying:

"Indeed you have long kept her from drinking, so she does not drink; so leave her, and let the buckets and the water-draw be cooled."
[[The line is in Lisan al-'Arab (root h-l-')]. Its transmission is "qad taalama" etc. He said: he drove the camels and cattle away from water, preventing them from coming to drink, and likewise a people kept others away from water. Ibn al-A'rabi said: A Qurayb said: There was a man in love with a woman, and he married her; then the women came to her, and some of them said to others: "Indeed you have long kept her from water, so she does not come." The line. The sijal is the plural of sajl, a great bucket filled with water (Lisan). The verse is evidence like the previous one, that "la tarid" permits both nominative and jussive by the interpretation that al-Farra' mentioned.]]

**The interpretation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿So it will come upon them suddenly, while they do not perceive (202). Then they will say, "Will we be reprieved?" (203). Then do they seek to hasten Our punishment? (204)﴾**

He, the Exalted, says: So there will come upon these deniers of this Qur'an the painful punishment, suddenly (baghtatan), meaning unexpectedly, ﴿while they do not perceive﴾, meaning they will not know beforehand of its coming until it overtakes them suddenly. ﴿Then they will say﴾ when it comes upon them suddenly, ﴿"Will we be reprieved?"﴾, that is: "Will the punishment be deferred from us, and will our terms be extended so that we may return (linu'ib) and turn penitently (nunib) to God from our polytheism and our disbelief in God, so that we may revert to belief in Him and turn penitently to obey Him?"

* *

And His saying: ﴿Then do they seek to hasten Our punishment?﴾

He, the Exalted, says: Do these polytheists seek to hasten Our punishment by their saying: "We will not believe you until you cause the sky to fall upon us in pieces, as you claimed" (Q. 17:92)?

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 26, verse 207:

The interpretation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿What did what they were given to enjoy avail them?﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Then there came upon them the punishment they had been promised, for their disbelief in Our signs and their denial of Our Messenger. ﴿What did it avail them﴾ means: what did the delay We granted them in their terms, and the enjoyment with which We gave them provision of life, avail them, since they did not repent of their polytheism? Did Our granting them that enjoyment increase them in anything but ruin (khabal)? Did it benefit them at all? Rather, it harmed them, through their increase in sins and their acquisition of crimes which, had they not been given enjoyment, they would not have acquired.

Ḥadīth: Yūnus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His saying: ﴿Have you considered, if We let them enjoy for years﴾ up to His saying ﴿what did what they were given to enjoy avail them?﴾, he said: These are the people of disbelief.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 26, verse 208–212:

The interpretation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And We did not destroy any town but that it had warners, as a reminder; and We were not unjust.﴾ [26:208–209] ﴿And the devils did not bring it down, nor is it befitting for them, nor are they able to.﴾ [26:210–211] ﴿Indeed, they are removed from hearing it.﴾ [26:212]

He, the Exalted, says: ﴿And We did not destroy any town﴾ from these towns described in these surahs ﴿but that it had warners﴾, meaning: only after We had sent to them messengers warning them of Our punishment for their disbelief and of Our wrath upon them. ﴿As a reminder﴾, meaning: they were warners who warned them, as a reminder to them and an admonition to them concerning that which would save them from Our punishment. There are two grammatical possibilities for ﴿dhikra﴾ (as a reminder): one is that it is in the accusative as a verbal noun (maṣdar) of the warning (indhār), as I have explained; the other is that it is in the nominative as a beginning (mubtada') [[It is permissible that His saying (dhikra) be nominative as a beginning, with the predicate omitted, meaning "a reminder for them." It is also permissible that it be nominative as the predicate of an omitted subject, its estimated form being "they," i.e., the warners, are a reminder for them.]], as if it were said: "a reminder."

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said something similar to what we have said regarding this.

Mention of those who said that:

* Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿And We did not destroy any town but that it had warners. As a reminder﴾, he said: "The messengers." Ibn Jurayj said: And His saying ﴿as a reminder﴾, he said: "The messengers."

* * *

His saying: ﴿And We were not unjust﴾

Meaning: We were not unjust to them in punishing and destroying them, for We only destroyed them when they transgressed against Us, denied Our blessing, and worshipped other than Us, after the proof had been established against them and the warning given, and the evidences had followed them, showing that they should not do that; yet they refused except to persist in error.

* * *

His saying: ﴿And the devils did not bring it down﴾

He, the Exalted, says: The devils did not bring down this Qur'an upon Muhammad (ﷺ), but rather the Trustworthy Spirit (al-Ruh al-Amin) brings it down with it. ﴿Nor is it befitting for them﴾, meaning: it is not befitting for the devils to bring it down upon him, nor is that suitable for them. ﴿Nor are they able to﴾, meaning: nor are they able to bring it down, for they cannot reach its hearing in the place it occupies in the heavens. ﴿Indeed, they are removed from hearing it﴾, meaning: indeed, the devils are removed from hearing the Qur'an from the place it occupies in the heavens; so how could they be able to bring it down?

The people of interpretation have said something similar to what we have said regarding the interpretation of this.

Mention of those who said that:

* Al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatada, regarding His saying ﴿And the devils did not bring it down﴾, he said: "This Qur'an." And regarding His saying ﴿Indeed, they are removed from hearing it﴾, he said: "Removed from hearing the heavens."

* Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Abu Sufyan narrated to me, from Ma'mar, from Qatada, similarly, except that he said: "Removed from hearing the Qur'an."

The readers (al-qurra') are unanimous on reading ﴿tanazzalat bihi al-shayatinu﴾ with a taa' and a raised nun (nazzalat... al-shayatinu), because the nun is original (asliyyah), and its singular is shaytan, just as the singular of al-basatin (gardens) is bustan. It is reported from al-Hasan that he used to read it: "wa-ma tanazzalat bihi al-shayatuna" with a waw, and that is a grammatical error (lahn). It should be that, if it is authentically transmitted from him, he imagined that it was analogous to al-muslimun and al-mu'minun; but that is far from this.

Mention of those who said that:

* Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿And We did not destroy any town but that it had warners. As a reminder﴾, he said: "The messengers." Ibn Jurayj said: And His saying ﴿as a reminder﴾, he said: "The messengers."

* * *

His saying: ﴿And We were not unjust﴾

Meaning: We were not unjust to them in punishing and destroying them, for We only destroyed them when they transgressed against Us, denied Our blessing, and worshipped other than Us, after the proof had been established against them and the warning given, and the evidences had followed them, showing that they should not do that; yet they refused except to persist in error.

* * *

His saying: ﴿And the devils did not bring it down﴾

He, the Exalted, says: The devils did not bring down this Qur'an upon Muhammad (ﷺ), but rather the Trustworthy Spirit (al-Ruh al-Amin) brings it down with it. ﴿Nor is it befitting for them﴾, meaning: it is not befitting for the devils to bring it down upon him, nor is that suitable for them. ﴿Nor are they able to﴾, meaning: nor are they able to bring it down, for they cannot reach its hearing in the place it occupies in the heavens. ﴿Indeed, they are removed from hearing it﴾, meaning: indeed, the devils are removed from hearing the Qur'an from the place it occupies in the heavens; so how could they be able to bring it down?

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿So do not invoke with Allah any other god, or you will be among those punished﴾ [26:213] ﴿And warn your closest kinsmen﴾ [26:214] ﴿And lower your wing to those who follow you of the believers﴾ [26:215].

His words, exalted is His remembrance, to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): ﴿So do not invoke﴾, O Muhammad, ﴿with Allah any other god﴾, that is, do not worship along with Him any deity other than Him, ﴿or you will be among those punished﴾, meaning that there will befall you the punishment that befell those who opposed Our command and worshipped other than Us.

* *

As for His words: ﴿And warn your closest kinsmen﴾

His words, may His praise be exalted, to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): And warn your kinsmen from your people who are nearest to you in blood, and caution them against Our punishment lest it befall them because of their disbelief.

It is mentioned that when this verse was revealed, he began with the sons of his grandfather ʿAbd al-Muttalib and his offspring, cautioning and warning them.

The narrations concerning this:

• Ahmad ibn al-Miqdam narrated to me, saying: Muhammad ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman told us, saying: Hisham ibn ʿUrwah told us, from his father, from ʿĀʾishah, who said: When this verse was revealed, ﴿And warn your closest kinsmen﴾, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O Safiyyah daughter of ʿAbd al-Muttalib, O Fatimah daughter of Muhammad, O sons of ʿAbd al-Muttalib, I possess nothing for you against Allah. Ask me of my wealth whatever you wish."

• Ibn Wakiʿ narrated to us, saying: My father and Yunus ibn Bukayr told me, from Hisham ibn ʿUrwah, from his father, from ʿĀʾishah, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), with similar wording.

• Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Hakkam told us, saying: ʿAnbasah told us, from Hisham ibn ʿUrwah, from his father, who said: When ﴿And warn your closest kinsmen﴾ was revealed, the Prophet (ﷺ) stood and said: "O Fatimah daughter of Muhammad, and O Safiyyah daughter of ʿAbd al-Muttalib," then he mentioned something similar to the hadith of Ibn al-Miqdam.

• Yunus ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla narrated to me, saying: Salamah told us, saying: ʿAqil said: Al-Zuhri told me, saying: Saʿid ibn al-Musayyab and Abu Salamah ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman said: Abu Hurayrah said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), when ﴿And warn your closest kinsmen﴾ was revealed to him, said: "O assembly of Quraysh, purchase your souls from Allah. I cannot avail you anything against Allah. O sons of ʿAbd Manaf, I cannot avail you anything against Allah. O ʿAbbas ibn ʿAbd al-Muttalib, I cannot avail you anything against Allah. O Fatimah daughter of the Messenger of Allah, I cannot avail you anything against Allah. Ask me whatever you wish; I cannot avail you anything against Allah."

• Muhammad ibn ʿAbd al-Malik narrated to me, saying: Abu al-Yaman told us, saying: Shuʿayb informed us, from al-Zuhri, who said: Saʿid ibn al-Musayyab and Abu Salamah ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman informed me that Abu Hurayrah said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), when it was revealed to him, ﴿And warn your closest kinsmen﴾, said: "O assembly of Quraysh, purchase your souls from Allah," then he mentioned something similar to the hadith of Yunus from Salamah, except that he added in it: "O Safiyyah, aunt of the Messenger of Allah, I cannot avail you anything against Allah," and he did not mention Fatimah in his hadith.

• Yunus narrated to me, saying: Salamah ibn Rawh told us, saying: ʿAqil said: Ibn Shihab told me that when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was sent down ﴿And warn your closest kinsmen﴾, he gathered the Quraysh, then came to them and said to them: "Is there a stranger among you?" They said: "No, except the son of our sister, whom we see only as one of us." He said: "He is of you." Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) admonished them, and at the end of his speech he said to them: "I will not know that you will come on the Day of Resurrection driving the Hereafter, while the people come to me driving the world."

• Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Yunus informed me, from Ibn Shihab: Saʿid ibn al-Musayyab and Abu Salamah ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman informed me that Abu Hurayrah said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), when ﴿And warn your closest kinsmen﴾ was revealed to him, said: "O assembly of Quraysh, purchase your souls from Allah. I cannot avail you anything against Allah. O sons of ʿAbd al-Muttalib, I cannot avail you anything against Allah. O ʿAbbas ibn ʿAbd al-Muttalib, I cannot avail you anything against Allah. O Safiyyah, aunt of the Messenger of Allah, I cannot avail you anything against Allah. O Fatimah daughter of Muhammad, ask me whatever you wish; I cannot avail you anything against Allah."

• Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla narrated to us, saying: Al-Muʿtamir told us, saying: I heard al-Hajjaj narrate, from ʿAbd al-Malik ibn ʿUmayr, from Musa ibn Talhah, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), that he said: When Allah revealed ﴿And warn your closest kinsmen﴾, the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O assembly of Quraysh, save yourselves from the Fire. O Fatimah daughter of Muhammad, save yourself from the Fire. Indeed, you have kinship (with me), which I will keep connected with its moisture."

• Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Abu Usamah told us, from Zaʾidah, from ʿAbd al-Malik ibn ʿUmayr, from Musa ibn Talhah, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: When this verse was revealed, ﴿And warn your closest kinsmen﴾, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) called Quraysh, addressing them in general and in particular, and said: "O assembly of Quraysh, purchase your souls from Allah. O assembly of the Banu Kaʿb ibn Luʾayy, O assembly of the Banu ʿAbd Manaf, O assembly of the Banu Hashim, O assembly of the Banu ʿAbd al-Muttalib," saying to each of them: "Save yourselves from the Fire. O Fatimah daughter of Muhammad, save yourself from the Fire, for I, by Allah, cannot avail you anything against Allah. Indeed, you have kinship (with me), which I will keep connected with its moisture."

• Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla narrated to us, saying: Al-Muʿtamir told us, from his father, who said: Abu ʿUthman told us, from Zuhayr ibn ʿAmr and Qabisah ibn Mukhariq, that they both said: Allah sent down upon the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ): ﴿And warn your closest kinsmen﴾, so he told us about the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) that he climbed a rock on a mountain, and climbed to its highest point a stone, then said: "O family of ʿAbd Manaf, O morning alarm! Indeed, I am a warner. My example and yours is that of a man who came upon an army, and feared for his family, so he went to watch over them [[It is said: rabaʾa al-qawm yarbauhum, and rabaʾa lahum, when he stood at a high place and looked far, watching for an enemy or a raiding army or the like]], and feared they would outrun him to his family, so he began to shout to them: 'O morning alarm!'" Or as he said.

• Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Wahhab and Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar told us, from ʿAwf, from Qasamah ibn Zuhayr, who said: It reached me that when ﴿And warn your closest kinsmen﴾ was revealed to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), he came, placed his finger in his ear, raised his voice, and said: "O sons of ʿAbd Manaf, O morning alarm!"

He said: Abu ʿAsim told me, saying: ʿAwf told us, from Qasamah ibn Zuhayr, who said: I think he narrated it from al-Ashʿari, from the Prophet (ﷺ), with similar wording.

• ʿAbd Allah ibn Abi Ziyad narrated to me, saying: Abu Zayd al-Ansari Saʿd ibn Aws told us, from ʿAwf, who said: Qasamah ibn Zuhayr said: al-Ashʿari told me, saying: When it was revealed, then he mentioned something similar, except that he said: he placed his two fingers in his two ears.

• Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Numayr told us, from al-Aʿmash, from ʿAmr ibn Murrah, from Saʿid ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: When this verse was revealed, ﴿And warn your closest kinsmen﴾, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stood on al-Safa and called out: "O morning alarm!" The people gathered to him, some coming in person and others sending their messengers. He said: "O sons of Hashim, O sons of ʿAbd al-Muttalib, O sons of Fihr, O sons of... O sons of... Tell me, if I informed you that cavalry at the foot of this mountain intended to raid you, would you believe me?" They said: "Yes." He said: "Then I am a warner to you before a severe punishment." Abu Lahab said: "Perdition to you for the rest of the day! Did you call us only for this?" So there was revealed: ﴿Perish the hands of Abu Lahab, and perish he﴾.

• Abu Kurayb and Abu al-Sa'ib narrated to us, both saying: Abu Muʿawiyah told us, from al-Aʿmash, from ʿAmr ibn Murrah, from Saʿid ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: One day the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) ascended al-Safa and said: "O morning alarm!" The Quraysh gathered to him and said to him: "What is the matter with you?" He said: "Tell me, if I informed you that the enemy would attack you at dawn or at dusk, would you not believe me?" They said: "Yes." He said: "Then I am a warner to you before a severe punishment." Abu Lahab said: "Perdition to you! Is it for this that you called us or gathered us?" So Allah revealed: ﴿Perish the hands of Abu Lahab﴾ ... to the end of the surah.

• Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Abu Usamah told us, from al-Aʿmash, from ʿAmr ibn Murrah, from Saʿid ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: When this verse was revealed, ﴿And warn your closest kinsmen, and your people among the sincere﴾, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went out until he climbed al-Safa and called out: "O morning alarm!" They said: "Who is this calling out?" They said: "Muhammad." So they gathered to him, and he said: "O sons of so-and-so, O sons of so-and-so, O sons of ʿAbd al-Muttalib, O sons of ʿAbd Manaf." They gathered to him, and he said: "Tell me, if I informed you that cavalry was coming out at the foot of this mountain, would you believe me?" They said: "We have not tested you as a liar." He said: "Then I am a warner to you before a severe punishment." Abu Lahab said: "Perdition to you! Did you gather us only for this?" Then he stood up, and this surah was revealed: ﴿Perish the hands of Abu Lahab, and perish he﴾, and he has perished. Thus al-Aʿmash recited it, to the end of the surah.

• Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Abu Muʿawiyah ibn Hisham told us, from Sufyan, from Habib, from Saʿid, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: When ﴿And warn your closest kinsmen﴾ was revealed, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went out, stood on al-Safa, and said: "O morning alarm!"

• He said: Khalid ibn ʿAmr narrated to us, saying: Sufyan al-Thawri told us, from Habib ibn Abi Thabit, from Saʿid ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: When ﴿And warn your closest kinsmen﴾ was revealed, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stood on al-Safa and said: "O morning alarm!" Then he began enumerating them: "O sons of so-and-so, and O sons of so-and-so, and O sons of ʿAbd Manaf."

• Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir told us, from Mughirah, from ʿAmr ibn Murrah al-Jamali, who said: When it was revealed, ﴿And warn your closest kinsmen﴾, he went to a mountain and began calling out: "O morning alarm!" Those who were quick among the people came to him, and those who were slow sent messengers to him, who began coming, following the sound. When they reached him, he said: "Among you is one who came to look, and among you is one who sent someone to look, to see who the caller is." When they gathered and grew numerous, he said: "Tell me, if I informed you that cavalry would attack you at dawn from this mountain, would you believe me?" They said: "Yes, we have not tested you as a liar." He then recited to them these verses that had been revealed, and warned them as he was commanded, and began calling out: "O Quraysh, O Banu Hashim," until he said: "O Banu ʿAbd al-Muttalib, I am a warner to you before a severe punishment."

• Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir told us, from ʿAmr, that he used to recite: ﴿And warn your closest kinsmen, and your people, the sincere ones﴾.

• He said: Salamah told us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ishaq told me, from ʿAbd al-Ghaffar ibn al-Qasim, from al-Minhal ibn ʿAmr, from ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Harith ibn Nawfal ibn al-Harith ibn ʿAbd al-Muttalib, from ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAbbas, from ʿAli ibn Abi Talib, who said: When this verse was revealed upon the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), ﴿And warn your closest kinsmen﴾, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) called me and said to me: "O ʿAli, indeed Allah has commanded me to warn my closest kinsmen." He said: "I was distressed by this, and I knew that if I called them to this matter, I would see from them what I dislike. So I remained silent until Jibril came and said: O Muhammad, if you do not do what you are commanded, your Lord will punish you. So prepare for us a sa' of food, put upon it the leg of a sheep, fill for us a bowl of milk, then gather for me the sons of ʿAbd al-Muttalib, so that I may speak to them and convey to them what I have been commanded." So I did what he commanded me, then I invited them to him. They were that day forty men, more or less by one, including his paternal uncles: Abu Talib, Hamzah, al-ʿAbbas, and Abu Lahab. When they gathered to him, he called for the food I had prepared for them, and I brought it. When I set it down, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) took a piece of meat [[In (al-Lisan: h-d-h): "I gave him a hidhyah of meat," and hadhah and fidhlah, all of this when cut lengthwise. It is also said: it is a small piece]] and tore it with his teeth, then threw it into the sides of the dish, and said: "Take it in the name of Allah." The people ate until they had no need of anything, and I saw nothing but the places of their hands. By Allah, by whose hand my soul is, if one man would eat what I had prepared for all of them. Then he said: "Give the people to drink," so I brought them that bowl, and they drank until they were all satisfied from it, and by Allah, if one man among them would drink the like of it. When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) wished to speak to them, Abu Lahab hastened to speech and said: "How great is the sorcery your companion has cast upon you!" [[In (al-Lisan: h-d-d) and in the hadith: "that Abu Lahab said: 'How great is what your companion has sorcerised you with.'" Lahada is an expression of wonder, said of a man: how strong he is. I say: it is like our saying: how strong was what so-and-so said, meaning how strong]] So the people dispersed, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did not speak to them. He said: "Tomorrow, O ʿAli, this man has forestalled me in what you have heard of the speech, so the people dispersed before I could speak to them. • Muhammad ibn ʿAbd al-Malik narrated to me, saying: Abu al-Yaman told us, saying: Shuʿayb informed us, from al-Zuhri, who said: Saʿid ibn al-Musayyab and Abu Salamah ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman informed me that Abu Hurayrah said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), when it was revealed to him, ﴿And warn your closest kinsmen﴾, said: "O assembly of Quraysh, purchase your souls from Allah," then he mentioned something similar to the hadith of Yunus from Salamah, except that he added in it: "O Safiyyah, aunt of the Messenger of Allah, I cannot avail you anything against Allah," and he did not mention Fatimah in his hadith.

• Yunus narrated to me, saying: Salamah ibn Rawh told us, saying: ʿAqil said: Ibn Shihab told me that when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was sent down ﴿And warn your closest kinsmen﴾, he gathered the Quraysh, then came to them and said to them: "Is there a stranger among you?" They said: "No, except the son of our sister, whom we see only as one of us." He said: "He is of you." Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) admonished them, and at the end of his speech he said to them: "I will not know that you will come on the Day of Resurrection driving the Hereafter, while the people come to me driving the world."

• Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Yunus informed me, from Ibn Shihab: Saʿid ibn al-Musayyab and Abu Salamah ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman informed me that Abu Hurayrah said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), when ﴿And warn your closest kinsmen﴾ was revealed to him, said: "O assembly of Quraysh, purchase your souls from Allah. I cannot avail you anything against Allah. O sons of ʿAbd al-Muttalib, I cannot avail you anything against Allah. O ʿAbbas ibn ʿAbd al-Muttalib, I cannot avail you anything against Allah. O Safiyyah, aunt of the Messenger of Allah, I cannot avail you anything against Allah. O Fatimah daughter of Muhammad, ask me whatever you wish; I cannot avail you anything against Allah."

• Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla narrated to us, saying: Al-Muʿtamir told us, saying: I heard al-Hajjaj narrate, from ʿAbd al-Malik ibn ʿUmayr, from Musa ibn Talhah, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), that he said: When Allah revealed ﴿And warn your closest kinsmen﴾, the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O assembly of Quraysh, save yourselves from the Fire. O Fatimah daughter of Muhammad, save yourself from the Fire. Indeed, you have kinship (with me), which I will keep connected with its moisture."

• Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Abu Usamah told us, from Zaʾidah, from ʿAbd al-Malik ibn ʿUmayr, from Musa ibn Talhah, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: When this verse was revealed, ﴿And warn your closest kinsmen﴾, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) called Quraysh, addressing them in general and in particular, and said: "O assembly of Quraysh, purchase your souls from Allah. O assembly of the Banu Kaʿb ibn Luʾayy, O assembly of the Banu ʿAbd Manaf, O assembly of the Banu Hashim, O assembly of the Banu ʿAbd al-Muttalib," saying to each of them: "Save yourselves from the Fire. O Fatimah daughter of Muhammad, save yourself from the Fire, for I, by Allah, cannot avail you anything against Allah. Indeed, you have kinship (with me), which I will keep connected with its moisture."

• Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla narrated to us, saying: Al-Muʿtamir told us, from his father, who said: Abu ʿUthman told us, from Zuhayr ibn ʿAmr and Qabisah ibn Mukhariq, that they both said: Allah sent down upon the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ): ﴿And warn your closest kinsmen﴾, so he told us about the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) that he climbed a rock on a mountain, and climbed to its highest point a stone, then said: "O family of ʿAbd Manaf, O morning alarm! Indeed, I am a warner. My example and yours is that of a man who came upon an army, and feared for his family, so he went to watch over them [[It is said: rabaʾa al-qawm yarbauhum, and rabaʾa lahum, when he stood at a high place and looked far, watching for an enemy or a raiding army or the like]], and feared they would outrun him to his family, so he began to shout to them: 'O morning alarm!'" Or as he said.

• Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Wahhab and Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar told us, from ʿAwf, from Qasamah ibn Zuhayr, who said: It reached me that when ﴿And warn your closest kinsmen﴾ was revealed to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), he came, placed his finger in his ear, raised his voice, and said: "O sons of ʿAbd Manaf, O morning alarm!"

He said: Abu ʿAsim told me, saying: ʿAwf told us, from Qasamah ibn Zuhayr, who said: I think he narrated it from al-Ashʿari, from the Prophet (ﷺ), with similar wording.

• ʿAbd Allah ibn Abi Ziyad narrated to me, saying: Abu Zayd al-Ansari Saʿd ibn Aws told us, from ʿAwf, who said: Qasamah ibn Zuhayr said: al-Ashʿari told me, saying: When it was revealed, then he mentioned something similar, except that he said: he placed his two fingers in his two ears.

• Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Numayr told us, from al-Aʿmash, from ʿAmr ibn Murrah, from Saʿid ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: When this verse was revealed, ﴿And warn your closest kinsmen﴾, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stood on al-Safa and called out: "O morning alarm!" The people gathered to him, some coming in person and others sending their messengers. He said: "O sons of Hashim, O sons of ʿAbd al-Muttalib, O sons of Fihr, O sons of... O sons of... Tell me, if I informed you that cavalry at the foot of this mountain intended to raid you, would you believe me?" They said: "Yes." He said: "Then I am a warner to you before a severe punishment." Abu Lahab said: "Perdition to you for the rest of the day! Did you call us only for this?" So there was revealed: ﴿Perish the hands of Abu Lahab, and perish he﴾.

• Abu Kurayb and Abu al-Sa'ib narrated to us, both saying: Abu Muʿawiyah told us, from al-Aʿmash, from ʿAmr ibn Murrah, from Saʿid ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: One day the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) ascended al-Safa and said: "O morning alarm!" The Quraysh gathered to him and said to him: "What is the matter with you?" He said: "Tell me, if I informed you that the enemy would attack you at dawn or at dusk, would you not believe me?" They said: "Yes." He said: "Then I am a warner to you before a severe punishment." Abu Lahab said: "Perdition to you! Is it for this that you called us or gathered us?" So Allah revealed: ﴿Perish the hands of Abu Lahab﴾ ... to the end of the surah.

• Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Abu Usamah told us, from al-Aʿmash, from ʿAmr ibn Murrah, from Saʿid ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: When this verse was revealed, ﴿And warn your closest kinsmen, and your people among the sincere﴾, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went out until he climbed al-Safa and called out: "O morning alarm!" They said: "Who is this calling out?" They said: "Muhammad." So they gathered to him, and he said: "O sons of so-and-so, O sons of so-and-so, O sons of ʿAbd al-Muttalib, O sons of ʿAbd Manaf." They gathered to him, and he said: "Tell me, if I informed you that cavalry was coming out at the foot of this mountain, would you believe me?" They said: "We have not tested you as a liar." He said: "Then I am a warner to you before a severe punishment." Abu Lahab said: "Perdition to you! Did you gather us only for this?" Then he stood up, and this surah was revealed: ﴿Perish the hands of Abu Lahab, and perish he﴾, and he has perished. Thus al-Aʿmash recited it, to the end of the surah.

• Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Abu Muʿawiyah ibn Hisham told us, from Sufyan, from Habib, from Saʿid, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: When ﴿And warn your closest kinsmen﴾ was revealed, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went out, stood on al-Safa, and said: "O morning alarm!"

• He said: Khalid ibn ʿAmr narrated to us, saying: Sufyan al-Thawri told us, from Habib ibn Abi Thabit, from Saʿid ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: When ﴿And warn your closest kinsmen﴾ was revealed, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stood on al-Safa and said: "O morning alarm!" Then he began enumerating them: "O sons of so-and-so, and O sons of so-and-so, and O sons of ʿAbd Manaf."

• Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir told us, from Mughirah, from ʿAmr ibn Murrah al-Jamali, who said: When it was revealed, ﴿And warn your closest kinsmen﴾, he went to a mountain and began calling out: "O morning alarm!" Those who were quick among the people came to him, and those who were slow sent messengers to him, who began coming, following the sound. When they reached him, he said: "Among you is one who came to look, and among you is one who sent someone to look, to see who the caller is." When they gathered and grew numerous, he said: "Tell me, if I informed you that cavalry would attack you at dawn from this mountain, would you believe me?" They said: "Yes, we have not tested you as a liar." He then recited to them these verses that had been revealed, and warned them as he was commanded, and began calling out: "O Quraysh, O Banu Hashim," until he said: "O Banu ʿAbd al-Muttalib, I am a warner to you before a severe punishment."

• Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir told us, from ʿAmr, that he used to recite: ﴿And warn your closest kinsmen, and your people, the sincere ones﴾.

• He said: Salamah told us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ishaq told me, from ʿAbd al-Ghaffar ibn al-Qasim, from al-Minhal ibn ʿAmr, from ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Harith ibn Nawfal ibn al-Harith ibn ʿAbd al-Muttalib, from ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAbbas, from ʿAli ibn Abi Talib, who said: When this verse was revealed upon the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), ﴿And warn your closest kinsmen﴾, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) called me and said to me: "O ʿAli, indeed Allah has commanded me to warn my closest kinsmen." He said: "I was distressed by this, and I knew that if I called them to this matter, I would see from them what I dislike. So I remained silent until Jibril came and said: O Muhammad, if you do not do what you are commanded, your Lord will punish you. So prepare for us a sa' of food, put upon it the leg of a sheep, fill for us a bowl of milk, then gather for me the sons of ʿAbd al-Muttalib, so that I may speak to them and convey to them what I have been commanded." So I did what he commanded me, then I invited them to him. They were that day forty men, more or less by one, including his paternal uncles: Abu Talib, Hamzah, al-ʿAbbas, and Abu Lahab. When they gathered to him, he called for the food I had prepared for them, and I brought it. When I set it down, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) took a piece of meat [[In (al-Lisan: h-d-h): "I gave him a hidhyah of meat," and hadhah and fidhlah, all of this when cut lengthwise. It is also said: it is a small piece]] and tore it with his teeth, then threw it into the sides of the dish, and said: "Take it in the name of Allah." The people ate until they had no need of anything, and I saw nothing but the places of their hands. By Allah, by whose hand my soul is, if one man would eat what I had prepared for all of them. Then he said: "Give the people to drink," so I brought them that bowl, and they drank until they were all satisfied from it, and by Allah, if one man among them would drink the like of it. When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) wished to speak to them, Abu Lahab hastened to speech and said: "How great is the sorcery your companion has cast upon you!" [[In (al-Lisan: h-d-d) and in the hadith: "that Abu Lahab said: 'How great is what your companion has sorcerised you with.'" Lahada is an expression of wonder, said of a man: how strong he is. I say: it is like our saying: how strong was what so-and-so said, meaning how strong]] So the people dispersed, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did not speak to them. He said: "Tomorrow, O ʿAli, this man has forestalled me in what you have heard of the speech, so the people dispersed before I could speak to them. Prepare for us food like what you prepared, then gather them for me." He said: So I did, then I gathered them, then he called for the food, and I brought it to them. He did as he had done the day before, and they ate until they had no need of anything. He said: "Give them to drink," so I brought them that bowl, and they drank until they were all satisfied from it. Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) spoke, and said: "O sons of ʿAbd al-Muttalib, by Allah, I do not know of a young man among the Arabs who has brought his people anything better than what I have brought you. I have brought you the good of this world and the Hereafter, and Allah has commanded me to call you to it. Which of you will support me in this matter, on condition that he be my brother," and such and such? He said: The people all held back from it, and I said, though I was the youngest of them in age, weakest of them in eyes, largest of them in belly, and thinnest of them in calves: "I, O Prophet of Allah, will be your vizier." So he took hold of my neck, then said: "Indeed, this is my brother," and such and such, "so listen to him and obey him." He said: So the people rose laughing, saying to Abu Talib: "He has commanded you to listen to your son and obey him!"

• Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah told us, saying: Ishaq told me, from ʿAmr ibn ʿUbayd, from al-Hasan ibn Abi al-Hasan, who said: When this verse was revealed upon the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), ﴿And warn your closest kinsmen﴾, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stood in al-Abtah and said: "O sons of ʿAbd al-Muttalib, O sons of ʿAbd Manaf, O sons of Qusayy." He said: Then he called out the clans of Quraysh clan by clan, until he passed over all of them: "Indeed, I call you to Allah, and I warn you of His punishment."

• Muhammad ibn Saʿd narrated to me, saying: My father told me, saying: My paternal uncle told me, saying: My father told me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding His words: ﴿And warn your closest kinsmen﴾, he said: Muhammad was commanded to warn his people, beginning with his family and his clan. [He said:] ﴿But your people denied it, while it is the truth﴾.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 26, verse 213–215 (part 2 of 2):

⁕ Al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Maʿmar informed us, from Hisham ibn ʿUrwah, from his father, who said: When the verse ﴿And warn your closest kinsmen﴾ was revealed, the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "O Fatimah, daughter of Muhammad! O Safiyyah, daughter of ʿAbd al-Muttalib! Save yourselves from the Fire, even if it is with half a date."

⁕ I was told by al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Muʿadh say: ʿUbayd informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say, concerning His words ﴿And warn your closest kinsmen﴾: He began with his own household and clan.

⁕ Al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Maʿmar informed us, from Qatadah, who said: When the verse ﴿And warn your closest kinsmen﴾ was revealed, the Prophet (ﷺ) gathered the Banu Hashim and said: "O Banu Hashim, I would not want to find you coming to me carrying the world while the people come carrying the Hereafter. Indeed, my allies from among you are the God-fearing. So save yourselves from the Fire, even if it is with half a date."

⁕ Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Juraij, who said: When this verse was revealed, he began with his own household and clan. He said: This was difficult for the Muslims, so God the Exalted revealed: ﴿And lower your wing to those who follow you among the believers﴾.

* *

His words ﴿And lower your wing﴾:
He means: soften your side and your speech ﴿to those who follow you among the believers﴾.
As:
⁕ Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His words ﴿And lower your wing to those who follow you among the believers﴾: He says: be gentle with them.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 26, verse 216–220:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So if they disobey you, say, "Indeed, I am disassociated from what you do. And rely upon the Exalted in Might, the Merciful, Who sees you when you stand [for prayer] and your movement among those who prostrate. Indeed, it is He who is the Hearing, the Knowing."﴾

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: If your closest kinsmen, whom I commanded you to warn, disobey you, O Muhammad, and refuse except to persist in worshipping idols and associating others with the Most Merciful, then say to them: ﴿Indeed, I am disassociated from what you do﴾, that is, from worshipping idols and from disobeying the Creator of creatures. ﴿And rely upon the Exalted in Might﴾, in His vengeance upon His enemies, ﴿the Merciful﴾ toward whoever turns to Him in repentance and repents from his sins.

﴿Who sees you when you stand﴾ means: Who sees you when you stand up for your prayer.

Mujahid used to say concerning its interpretation:

* Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, regarding his saying: ﴿Who sees you when you stand﴾, he said: "Wherever you are."

﴿And your movement among those who prostrate﴾ — the people of interpretation differed regarding its interpretation. Some of them said: the meaning of that is: and He sees your movement in your prayer when you stand, then bow, and when you prostrate.

Those who said that:

* Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding his saying: ﴿And your movement among those who prostrate﴾, he said: your standing, your bowing, and your prostration.

* Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, saying: I heard my father and Ali ibn Badhimah narrating from Ikrimah regarding his saying: ﴿who sees you when you stand and your movement among those who prostrate﴾, he said: his standing, his bowing, and his prostration.

* al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, saying: Ikrimah said, regarding his saying: ﴿And your movement among those who prostrate﴾, he said: standing, prostrating, bowing, and sitting.

Others said: rather, the meaning of that is: and He sees your movement among those who pray, and your seeing of those behind you among them just as you see those in front of you among them.

Those who said that:

* Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Layth, from Mujahid: ﴿And your movement among those who prostrate﴾, he used to see behind him just as he saw in front of him.

* Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding his saying: ﴿And your movement among those who prostrate﴾, he said: "Those who pray; he used to see those behind him during the prayer."

* al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, regarding his saying: ﴿And your movement among those who prostrate﴾, he said: "Those who pray; he used to see those behind him during the prayer."

Others said: rather, the meaning of that is: and your movement with those who prostrate, that is, your turning about with them in sitting, standing, and sitting.

Those who said that:

* al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, saying: Ibn Jurayj said: Ata al-Khurasani informed me, from Ibn Abbas, who said: ﴿And your movement among those who prostrate﴾, he said: He sees you while you move among those who prostrate, standing, and sitting with them.

* al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, regarding his saying: ﴿And your movement among those who prostrate﴾, he said: among those who pray.

* Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding his saying: (And your movement among those who prostrate), he said: among those who prostrate, the worshippers.

Others said: rather, the meaning of that is: and He sees your conduct among the people.

Those who said that:

* Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Yahya narrated to us, saying: Rabi'ah ibn Kulthum narrated to us, saying: I asked al-Hasan about his saying: ﴿And your movement among those who prostrate﴾, and he said: among the people.

Others said: rather, the meaning of that is: and your conduct in your affairs as the prophets before you used to do, and "those who prostrate," according to the one who holds this view, are the prophets.

Those who said that:

* Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Yaman narrated to us, from Ash'ath, from Ja'far, from Sa'id, regarding his saying: ﴿Who sees you﴾ ... the verse, he said: as the prophets before you used to do.

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: The most correct of these views regarding its interpretation is the view of the one who said its interpretation is: and He sees your movement with those who prostrate in their prayer along with you, when you stand with them and bow and prostrate, because that is the apparent meaning of it. As for the view of the one who directed it to mean: your movement among the people, it is a view far from what is understood from the apparent recitation, although it has a basis, because although there is nothing but that its shadow prostrates to Allah, it is not understood from the speaker's saying: "So-and-so is with those who prostrate," or "among those who prostrate," that he is with the people or among them; rather, what is understood by that is that he is with a people who prostrate in the well-known prostration. Directing the meanings of the words of Allah to the more prevalent is better than directing them to the more unusual.

Likewise, regarding the view of the one who said its meaning is: you turn about among the eyes of those who prostrate, although it has a basis, that is not the apparent meaning of it.

So the interpretation of the speech is therefore: And rely upon the Exalted in Might, the Merciful, Who sees you when you stand for your prayer, and sees your movement among those who follow you in it, between standing, bowing, prostration and sitting.

* *

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, it is He who is the Hearing, the Knowing﴾

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: Indeed your Lord is the Hearer of your recitation, O Muhammad, and of your remembrance in your prayer of what you recite and mention, the Knowing of what you do in it and what those who move in it along with you, following you, do. He says: so chant the Qur'an in it, and observe its limits, for you are under the sight and hearing of your Lord.
