The commentary on the words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And the poets—those who go astray follow them. Have you not seen that they wander distractedly in every valley? And that they say what they do not do? Except those who believe and do righteous deeds and remember Allah often and defend themselves after being wronged. And those who wronged will know what [manner of] return they will be returned to.﴾

Allah, the Exalted, says: The poets are followed by the people of error, not the people of guidance and right direction.

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) differed concerning those described as "those who go astray" in this place. Some of them said: they are the transmitters of poetry (ruwat al-shi'r).

Mention of who said this:

Al-Hasan ibn Yazid al-Tahhan narrated to me, saying: Ishaq ibn Mansur narrated to us, saying: Qays narrated to us, from Ya'la, from Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas; and Abu Kurayb narrated to me, saying: Talq ibn Ghannam narrated to us, from Qays; and Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn 'Atiyyah narrated to us, from Qays, from Ya'la ibn al-Nu'man, from Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding ﴿And the poets—those who go astray follow them﴾: he said: "the transmitters."

Others said: they are the devils (al-shayatin).

Mention of who said this:

Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿And the poets—those who go astray follow them﴾: "the devils."

al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, similarly.

al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿those who go astray follow them﴾: "The devils follow them."

Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Sa'id and 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, both saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Salamah ibn Kuhayl, from Ikrimah, regarding His saying ﴿And the poets—those who go astray follow them﴾: "The disobedient jinn."

Others said: they are the foolish ones, and they said: this was revealed concerning two men who engaged in mutual satire during the lifetime of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

Mention of who said this:

Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿And the poets—those who go astray follow them﴾ ... to the end of the verse, he said: There were two men during the lifetime of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): one of them from the Ansar, and the other from another people, and they satirized each other, and with each of them were misguided ones from his people, who were the foolish. So Allah said: ﴿And the poets—those who go astray follow them. Have you not seen that they wander distractedly in every valley?﴾

I heard from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His saying ﴿And the poets—those who go astray follow them﴾: There were two men during the lifetime of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): one of them from the Ansar, and the other from another people; they satirized each other, and with each of them were misguided ones from his people, and they were the foolish.

Others said: they are the misguided of the jinn and mankind.

Mention of who said this:

'Ali narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿And the poets—those who go astray follow them﴾: he said: They are the disbelievers, followed by the misguided of the jinn and mankind.

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding the word of Allah ﴿And the poets—those who go astray follow them﴾: "Those who go astray are the polytheists."

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of these sayings in terms of truth is that it be said what Allah, may His praise be exalted, said: that the poets of the polytheists are followed by the misguided among people, the rebellious devils, and the disobedient jinn. This is because Allah generalized with His saying ﴿And the poets—those who go astray follow them﴾ and did not specify some of the misguided over others; so it applies to all categories of the misguided that fall within the generality of the verse.

* *

His saying: ﴿Have you not seen that they wander distractedly in every valley?﴾

Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Have you not seen, O Muhammad, that they—meaning the poets—go in every valley, like one wandering aimlessly without purpose, rather deviating from the truth, and the path of right guidance, and the direct way.

This is only a parable Allah gave for them in their fabrication across the various modes in which they fabricate without right, praising some people falsely and satirizing others likewise with lies and falsehood.

The people of interpretation said things similar to what we have said.

Mention of who said this:

'Ali narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿Have you not seen that they wander distractedly in every valley?﴾ He says: in every idle talk they plunge.

Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿in every valley they wander distractedly﴾: "in every art they fabricate."

al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿Have you not seen that they are in every valley﴾: "art" ﴿wander distractedly﴾: "they say."

al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿in every valley they wander distractedly﴾: "They praise some people with falsehood and revile others with falsehood."

* *

His saying: ﴿And that they say what they do not do﴾

He says: that most of their speech is falsehood and lying.

As:

'Ali narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿And that they say what they do not do﴾: he says: most of their speech is lying.

By this is meant the poets of the polytheists.

As:

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd said: A man said to my father: "O Abu Usamah, what do you say about the word of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And the poets—those who go astray follow them. Have you not seen that they wander distractedly in every valley? And that they say what they do not do﴾?" My father said to him: "This is only about the poets of the polytheists, not the poets of the believers. Do you not see that He says: ﴿Except those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾ ... etc." He said: "You have relieved me, O Abu Usamah; may Allah relieve you."

* *

His saying: ﴿Except those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾

This is an exception from His saying ﴿And the poets—those who go astray follow them﴾ ... ﴿Except those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾. It is mentioned that this exception was revealed concerning the poets of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), such as Hassan ibn Thabit and Ka'b ibn Malik, and then it applies to everyone who has the attribute by which Allah described it.

Reports have come in accordance with what we have said.

Mention of who said this:

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah, 'Ali ibn Mujahid and Ibrahim ibn al-Mukhtar narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from Yazid ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Qusayt, from Abu al-Hasan Salim al-Barrad, freedman of Tamim al-Dari, who said: When ﴿And the poets—those who go astray follow them﴾ was revealed, Hassan ibn Thabit, 'Abd Allah ibn Rawahah and Ka'b ibn Malik came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) while they were weeping, and they said: "Allah knows, when He revealed this verse, that we are poets." So the Prophet (ﷺ) recited: ﴿Except those who believe and do righteous deeds and remember Allah often and defend themselves after being wronged. And those who wronged will know what [manner of] return they will be returned to.﴾

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, from some of his companions, from 'Ata' ibn Yasar, who said: ﴿And the poets—those who go astray follow them﴾ down to the end of the surah was revealed concerning Hassan ibn Thabit, 'Abd Allah ibn Rawahah and Ka'b ibn Malik.

He said: Yahya ibn Wadih narrated to us, from al-Husayn, from Yazid, from Ikrimah and Tawus, both said: ﴿And the poets—those who go astray follow them. Have you not seen that they wander distractedly in every valley? And that they say what they do not do﴾; so He abrogated part of that and made an exception, saying: ﴿Except those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾ ... the verse.

'Ali narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: Then He excepted from them, meaning the poets, the believers, saying: ﴿Except those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾.

al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Ibn 'Abbas said, and mentioned something similar.

al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah: ﴿Except those who believe and do righteous deeds and remember Allah often and defend themselves after being wronged﴾, he said: they are the Ansar who emigrated with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: 'Isa ibn Yunus narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from Yazid ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Qusayt, from Abu Hasan al-Barrad, who said: When ﴿And the poets—those who go astray follow them﴾ was revealed, then he mentioned something similar to the report of Ibn Humayd from Salamah.

* *

His saying: ﴿And remember Allah often﴾

The people of interpretation differed concerning the state of the remembrance by which Allah described these excepted poets. Some of them said: it refers to the condition of their speech and their dialogue with people. They said: the meaning of the statement is: and they remember Allah often in their speech.

Mention of who said this:

'Ali narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿Except those who believe and do righteous deeds and remember Allah often﴾: in their speech.

Others said: rather, it is in their poetry.

Mention of who said this:

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿and remember Allah often﴾: "They remember Allah in their poetry."

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of these sayings in terms of truth is that it be said: Allah described those He excepted from the believing poets with remembering Allah often, and He did not restrict their remembrance to one state over another in His Book or on the tongue of His Messenger; so their description is that they remember Allah often in all their states.

* *

His saying: ﴿And defend themselves after being wronged﴾

He says: and they took revenge on those of the polytheist poets who satirized them unjustly with their poetry and their satire of them, and their replying to what they satirized them with.

The people of interpretation said things similar to what we have said in interpreting this.

Mention of who said this:

'Ali narrated to me, saying: 'Abd Allah narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿And defend themselves after being wronged﴾: he said: They respond to the disbelievers who used to satirize the believers.

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying: ﴿and defend themselves from the polytheists after being wronged﴾.

It was said: all of this refers to the group I mentioned.

Mention of who said this:

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: 'Ali ibn Mujahid and Ibrahim ibn al-Mukhtar narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from Yazid ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Qusayt, from Abu al-Hasan Salim al-Barrad, freedman of Tamim al-Dari, who said: When ﴿And the poets—those who go astray follow them﴾ was revealed, Hassan ibn Thabit, 'Abd Allah ibn Rawahah and Ka'b ibn Malik came to the Prophet (ﷺ) while they were weeping, and they said: "Allah knows, when He revealed this verse, that we are poets." So the Prophet (ﷺ) recited: ﴿Except those who believe and do righteous deeds and remember Allah often and defend themselves after being wronged﴾.

al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: 'Isa ibn Yunus narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from Yazid ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Qusayt, from Abu Hasan al-Barrad, who said: When ﴿And the poets—those who go astray follow them﴾ was revealed, then he mentioned something similar.

Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿and defend themselves after being wronged﴾: "'Abd Allah ibn Rawahah and his companions."

al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid: ﴿and defend themselves after being wronged﴾: "'Abd Allah ibn Rawahah."

* *

His saying: ﴿And those who wronged will know﴾

Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, says: And those who wronged themselves by their polytheism with Allah from among the people of Makkah will know ﴿what [manner of] return they will be returned to﴾. That is: what place of return they will return to, and what final destination they will go back to after their deaths, for they will arrive at a Fire whose blaze will not be extinguished and whose flame will not subside.

The people of interpretation said things similar to what we have said regarding this.

Mention of who said this:

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah, 'Ali ibn Mujahid and Ibrahim ibn al-Mukhtar narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from Yazid ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Qusayt, from Abu al-Hasan Salim al-Barrad, freedman of Tamim al-Dari: ﴿And those who wronged will know what [manner of] return they will be returned to﴾: he means the people of Makkah.

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿And those who wronged will know what [manner of] return they will be returned to﴾: "And those who wronged among the polytheists will know what [manner of] return they will be returned to."

al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, similarly.

al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿those who go astray follow them﴾: "The devils follow them."

Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Sa'id and 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, both saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Salamah ibn Kuhayl, from Ikrimah, regarding His saying ﴿And the poets—those who go astray follow them﴾: "The disobedient jinn."

Others said: they are the foolish ones, and they said: this was revealed concerning two men who engaged in mutual satire during the lifetime of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

Mention of who said this:

Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿And the poets—those who go astray follow them﴾ ... to the end of the verse, he said: There were two men during the lifetime of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): one of them from the Ansar, and the other from another people, and they satirized each other, and with each of them were misguided ones from his people, who were the foolish. So Allah said: ﴿And the poets—those who go astray follow them. Have you not seen that they wander distractedly in every valley?﴾

I heard from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His saying ﴿And the poets—those who go astray follow them﴾: There were two men during the lifetime of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): one of them from the Ansar, and the other from another people; they satirized each other, and with each of them were misguided ones from his people, and they were the foolish.

Others said: they are the misguided of the jinn and mankind.

Mention of who said this:

'Ali narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿And the poets—those who go astray follow them﴾: he said: They are the disbelievers, followed by the misguided of the jinn and mankind.

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding the word of Allah ﴿And the poets—those who go astray follow them﴾: "Those who go astray are the polytheists."

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of these sayings in terms of truth is that it be said what Allah, may His praise be exalted, said: that the poets of the polytheists are followed by the misguided among people, the rebellious devils, and the disobedient jinn. This is because Allah generalized with His saying ﴿And the poets—those who go astray follow them﴾ and did not specify some of the misguided over others; so it applies to all categories of the misguided that fall within the generality of the verse.

* *

His saying: ﴿Have you not seen that they wander distractedly in every valley?﴾

Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Have you not seen, O Muhammad, that they—meaning the poets—go in every valley, like one wandering aimlessly without purpose, rather deviating from the truth, and the path of right guidance, and the direct way.

This is only a parable Allah gave for them in their fabrication across the various modes in which they fabricate without right, praising some people falsely and satirizing others likewise with lies and falsehood.

The people of interpretation said things similar to what we have said.

Mention of who said this:

'Ali narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿Have you not seen that they wander distractedly in every valley?﴾ He says: in every idle talk they plunge.

Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿in every valley they wander distractedly﴾: "in every art they fabricate."

al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿Have you not seen that they are in every valley﴾: "art" ﴿wander distractedly﴾: "they say."

al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿in every valley they wander distractedly﴾: "They praise some people with falsehood and revile others with falsehood."

* *

His saying: ﴿And that they say what they do not do﴾

He says: that most of their speech is falsehood and lying.

As:

'Ali narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿And that they say what they do not do﴾: he says: most of their speech is lying.

By this is meant the poets of the polytheists.

As:

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd said: A man said to my father: "O Abu Usamah, what do you say about the word of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And the poets—those who go astray follow them. Have you not seen that they wander distractedly in every valley? And that they say what they do not do﴾?" My father said to him: "This is only about the poets of the polytheists, not the poets of the believers. Do you not see that He says: ﴿Except those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾ ... etc." He said: "You have relieved me, O Abu Usamah; may Allah relieve you."

* *

His saying: ﴿Except those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾

This is an exception from His saying ﴿And the poets—those who go astray follow them﴾ ... ﴿Except those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾. It is mentioned that this exception was revealed concerning the poets of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), such as Hassan ibn Thabit and Ka'b ibn Malik, and then it applies to everyone who has the attribute by which Allah described it.

Reports have come in accordance with what we have said.

Mention of who said this:

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah, 'Ali ibn Mujahid and Ibrahim ibn al-Mukhtar narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from Yazid ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Qusayt, from Abu al-Hasan Salim al-Barrad, freedman of Tamim al-Dari, who said: When ﴿And the poets—those who go astray follow them﴾ was revealed, Hassan ibn Thabit, 'Abd Allah ibn Rawahah and Ka'b ibn Malik came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) while they were weeping, and they said: "Allah knows, when He revealed this verse, that we are poets." So the Prophet (ﷺ) recited: ﴿Except those who believe and do righteous deeds and remember Allah often and defend themselves after being wronged. And those who wronged will know what [manner of] return they will be returned to.﴾

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, from some of his companions, from 'Ata' ibn Yasar, who said: ﴿And the poets—those who go astray follow them﴾ down to the end of the surah was revealed concerning Hassan ibn Thabit, 'Abd Allah ibn Rawahah and Ka'b ibn Malik.

He said: Yahya ibn Wadih narrated to us, from al-Husayn, from Yazid, from Ikrimah and Tawus, both said: ﴿And the poets—those who go astray follow them. Have you not seen that they wander distractedly in every valley? And that they say what they do not do﴾; so He abrogated part of that and made an exception, saying: ﴿Except those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾ ... the verse.

'Ali narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: Then He excepted from them, meaning the poets, the believers, saying: ﴿Except those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾.

al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Ibn 'Abbas said, and mentioned something similar.

al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah: ﴿Except those who believe and do righteous deeds and remember Allah often and defend themselves after being wronged﴾, he said: they are the Ansar who emigrated with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: 'Isa ibn Yunus narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from Yazid ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Qusayt, from Abu Hasan al-Barrad, who said: When ﴿And the poets—those who go astray follow them﴾ was revealed, then he mentioned something similar to the report of Ibn Humayd from Salamah.

* *

His saying: ﴿And remember Allah often﴾

The people of interpretation differed concerning the state of the remembrance by which Allah described these excepted poets. Some of them said: it refers to the condition of their speech and their dialogue with people. They said: the meaning of the statement is: and they remember Allah often in their speech.

Mention of who said this:

'Ali narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿Except those who believe and do righteous deeds and remember Allah often﴾: in their speech.

Others said: rather, it is in their poetry.

Mention of who said this:

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿and remember Allah often﴾: "They remember Allah in their poetry."

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of these sayings in terms of truth is that it be said: Allah described those He excepted from the believing poets with remembering Allah often, and He did not restrict their remembrance to one state over another in His Book or on the tongue of His Messenger; so their description is that they remember Allah often in all their states.

* *

His saying: ﴿And defend themselves after being wronged﴾

He says: and they took revenge on those of the polytheist poets who satirized them unjustly with their poetry and their satire of them, and their replying to what they satirized them with.

The people of interpretation said things similar to what we have said in interpreting this.

Mention of who said this:

'Ali narrated to me, saying: 'Abd Allah narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿And defend themselves after being wronged﴾: he said: They respond to the disbelievers who used to satirize the believers.

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying: ﴿and defend themselves from the polytheists after being wronged﴾.

It was said: all of this refers to the group I mentioned.

Mention of who said this:

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: 'Ali ibn Mujahid and Ibrahim ibn al-Mukhtar narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from Yazid ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Qusayt, from Abu al-Hasan Salim al-Barrad, freedman of Tamim al-Dari, who said: When ﴿And the poets—those who go astray follow them﴾ was revealed, Hassan ibn Thabit, 'Abd Allah ibn Rawahah and Ka'b ibn Malik came to the Prophet (ﷺ) while they were weeping, and they said: "Allah knows, when He revealed this verse, that we are poets." So the Prophet (ﷺ) recited: ﴿Except those who believe and do righteous deeds and remember Allah often and defend themselves after being wronged﴾.

al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: 'Isa ibn Yunus narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from Yazid ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Qusayt, from Abu Hasan al-Barrad, who said: When ﴿And the poets—those who go astray follow them﴾ was revealed, then he mentioned something similar.

Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿and defend themselves after being wronged﴾: "'Abd Allah ibn Rawahah and his companions."

al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid: ﴿and defend themselves after being wronged﴾: "'Abd Allah ibn Rawahah."

* *

His saying: ﴿And those who wronged will know﴾

Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, says: And those who wronged themselves by their polytheism with Allah from among the people of Makkah will know ﴿what [manner of] return they will be returned to﴾. That is: what place of return they will return to, and what final destination they will go back to after their deaths, for they will arrive at a Fire whose blaze will not be extinguished and whose flame will not subside.

The people of interpretation said things similar to what we have said regarding this.

Mention of who said this:

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah, 'Ali ibn Mujahid and Ibrahim ibn al-Mukhtar narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from Yazid ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Qusayt, from Abu al-Hasan Salim al-Barrad, freedman of Tamim al-Dari: ﴿And those who wronged will know what [manner of] return they will be returned to﴾: he means the people of Makkah.

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿And those who wronged will know what [manner of] return they will be returned to﴾: "And those who wronged among the polytheists will know what [manner of] return they will be returned to."

End of the commentary on Surat al-Shu'ara'
